## 0. How to use this document

1. Read §0 (measured baseline) and §1 (defect register). Those two sections are the *evidence*; the tasks in §2
   are only worth doing because of them.
2. Pick a wave from §6. Waves are ordered by dependency, not by taste.
3. Do not start a task without reading its **Guardrails** block — most of them exist because a plausible-looking
   fix would break a rule in `AGENTS.md` §5 or `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §3.
4. Every task ends with a **Gate** block. A task is not done when it looks right; it is done when its gate
   command passes and its evidence is pasted into `build/check-report.json`.
5. This plan deliberately contains **no estimates in hours** for the AI portion and rough ranges for human
   review only. Sizing is S (≤ 2 h of agent work), M (half a day), L (a day or more, usually split by chapter).
6. Nothing in this plan authorises editing `workspace_skills/`. All skills are read and invoked; their scripts
   are run from the scratchpad.

### What this baseline says in one paragraph

The content layer is strong: sources are cited, corrections are paired, numbers are asserted by script, the
glossary and the mistake-seed coverage are real. The *engineering* layer has small but real holes (7 invalid
HTML structures, two disagreeing gate runners, a silenced inspector). The *design* layer is competent but
anonymous — a dark masthead band, a boxed contents card, 357 buttons of equal weight, 16 diagrams all drawn to
the same 760-unit canvas at 13 px labels that shrink to ≈ 6 px on a phone. The *teaching* layer is dense and
honest but unevenly visual: seven chapters teach without a single diagram, and the four hardest chapters are the
ones with none.

## 1.1 What is already good and must survive

These are load-bearing. Any task that breaks one of them is rejected on review.

1. **Pairing discipline.** Every correction is `Avotā / Pareizi / Kāpēc` + id, in `div.pair` (62 of them),
   generated from `ledger.py`, never hand-written. `c_corrections` asserts all 61.
2. **Number discipline.** Every intermediate is `<span class="num" data-exact data-expr>`; 191 assertions in
   `check_numbers.py`; rounding rule stated once in ch13 and linked.
3. **Recall discipline.** Every question is a `<details>`; answers are never visible by default; 270 of them.
4. **No network.** One file, zero requests, opens from `file://`, prints with answers open.
5. **Terminology machine.** `terms.py` holds `CANON` / `BANNED` / `CONFUSABLE` / `APPROVED_PENDING` and the build
   refuses to write a violating page. New terms go in the machine, never into prose.
6. **Honest tagging.** `[D p.11]`, `papildinājums`, `[jāpārbauda]` are used, and the X-basis subset carries a named
   reference when verified.

## T01 — Terminology canonisation and Latvian grammar sweep

**Theme:** terminology · copy · correctness
**Priority:** P0 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 1 · **Owner skill:** `impeccable` (Read + `clarify` reference) with
`terms.py` as the machine · **Depends on:** nothing (do this first; every later task writes Latvian text)

### Evidence
- `Bieži kļūdas` ×45 — ungrammatical (F04).
- `Kur kļūdīties` ×22 — missing *var* (F05).
- `Molu karte` ×2 — banned use of *mols* as a thing (F06).
- `molaritāte*` ×15 against canonical *molārā koncentrācija*; `sārmains*` ×16 against *bāzisks*, with no role rule (F07).
- `—` ×13 where Latvian uses `–` (F08).
- `Atgriezieties pie` ×16 used as a heading with no object (F24).
- Two sentences left dangling outside their paragraph in `ch07:22` and `ch09:17` (F02) — the second one,
  *"Vai mainīs un uz kuru pusi, nosaka tas…"*, is also missing its subject (*pH*).

### Intent
Make one spelling per term, one grammatical block-name set, and make the machine refuse the old forms so the
sweep cannot silently regress on the next build. The reader should never see two names for one quantity, and a
Latvian teacher should not be able to find an error in the section headings alone.

### Definition of done
- [ ] `terms.py` `BANNED` contains every rejected variant below, each with a reason string and an allow-list for
      legitimate mentions (the appendix table that quotes the rejected form, the glossary contrast row).
- [ ] `build/check_text.py` exists and fails the build on: any `—`, any banned variant outside an allow-list, any
      heading in `HEADING_FIXES` still present, any paragraph beginning lowercase after a `</p>` stray.
- [ ] Heading counts after rebuild: `Biežākās kļūdas` = 45, `Kur var kļūdīties` = 22, `Priekšzināšanas` = 16,
      `Vielas daudzuma karte` = 2, `Bieži kļūdas` = 0, `Kur kļūdīties` = 0, `Atgriezieties pie` = 0.
- [ ] `molaritāte` survives only in the glossary as an alias in the "jauc ar" column, 0 uses in prose.
- [ ] Em dash count = 0; en dash count unchanged at ≥ 280.
- [ ] `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §3.2 and §4 and `AGENTS.md` §5 are updated in the same commit, because both currently
      *prescribe* the wrong heading (`Bieži kļūdas`) — the plan is the source of the error, not the page.
- [ ] A "Terminu lēmumi" table row is added to the appendix changelog for each change, with the id that motivated it.

### Task substeps
1. **Inventory and decide.** Export every heading and every candidate term with its count and first occurrence.
   Decide each one against `SOURCE_LEDGER.md` §2 + `AGENTS.md` §8 defaults. Write the decision table (see §5 of
   this plan) into `build/terms_decisions.md`.
2. **Mechanise.** Move decisions into `terms.py` (`CANON`, `BANNED`, `HEADING_FIXES`, `DASH`), fix the content
   files, and rebuild. No find-and-replace in the built HTML — it is generated.
3. **Audit and record.** Run the new `check_text.py`, diff heading counts, and paste the before/after table into
   `build/check-report.json` under a `text` step.

### Subtask 1.1 — Block-name grammar (headings)
- **1.1.a** Add `HEADING_FIXES = {"Bieži kļūdas": "Biežākās kļūdas", "Kur kļūdīties": "Kur var kļūdīties",
  "Atgriezieties pie": "Priekšzināšanas", "Molu karte": "Vielas daudzuma karte"}` to `terms.py`; `build_master.py`
  asserts the post-build count of each new form equals the pre-build count of the old form.
- **1.1.b** Rewrite the four affected block templates in `build_master.py` (mist block, work block, ret block,
  figure title) so the strings live in one place, not 45 times in content.
- **1.1.c** Re-render the four affected places at 1440 and 390 and confirm the heading does not wrap badly and the
  anchor ids (`#mist-…`, `#ret-…`) are unchanged, because 440 anchors are asserted by `c_anchors`.

### Subtask 1.2 — Quantity names
- **1.2.a** Add `molaritāte` → `molārā koncentrācija` to `BANNED` with allow-list `["glossary-alias"]`; the
  glossary row keeps *molaritāte* only in the "jauc ar / sinonīms, lietots ārstu tekstos" cell so a student who
  meets the word in a lab report can still find it.
- **1.2.b** Write the **role rule** for the *bāzisks / sārmains* family into `terms.py` as three separate entries:
  *bāziskais oksīds* (compound class), *bāziska vide / pH > 7* (solution), *sārms* (water-soluble hydroxide).
  Any prose use of *sārmains* must be inside a phrase naming a solution or a pH value; `check_text.py` asserts the
  pattern `sārmain\w*\s+(šķīdum|vide|asinis)` and flags bare uses.
- **1.2.c** Re-check the 16 existing uses one by one against that rule; rewrite those that mean "pH > 7" to
  *bāziska vide*, keep those that mean blood alkalinity (*asinis ir vāji sārmainas*) because that is the course's
  own D p.20 usage, and record the split in the changelog.

### Subtask 1.3 — Punctuation and dangling text
- **1.3.a** Replace the 13 em dashes with en dashes and add the rule to `typography.py` (`—` is a hard failure, not
  a WARN). Keep the lint baseline entry only for the en dash, which Latvian grammar needs.
- **1.3.b** Repair the two dangling sentences: `ch07:22` and `ch09:17`. Move the loose sentence inside the `lead`
  paragraph or give it its own `<p class="why1">`; restore the missing subject (`Vai pH mainīsies un uz kuru pusi,
  nosaka tas, no kādas skābes un bāzes sāls veidots.`).
- **1.3.c** Add a proofreading checklist to `build/README.md`: subject present, no calque block names, one term per
  quantity, no sentence outside a block element, no em dash, decimal comma, thin no-break space before units.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/build_master.py && python3 build/check_text.py && python3 build/check_terms.py
grep -c 'Biežākās kļūdas' Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html   # 45
grep -c '—' Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html                # 0
```

### Guardrails
- Do **not** "fix" quoted source text. If a source phrase is ungrammatical and is being quoted to show what the
  source says, it stays, inside the quotation marks, with its `[A p.N]` tag.
- Do **not** rename a term that `SOURCE_LEDGER.md` §2 marks **[apstiprināt]** without listing it in the open
  questions (§8). Those six stay as defaults until the user confirms.
- The em-dash rule must not break the `typography.py` thousands-separator or unit-space checks; run all of them.

## T02 — DOM structure repair and a parser gate

**Theme:** polish out mistakes · engineering
**Priority:** P0 · **Effort:** S · **Wave:** 1 · **Owner skill:** `audit` (technical pass), `break-ui` for the
stress cases · **Depends on:** nothing

### Evidence
- 4 unclosed `<dl class="calc">`: `ch06:12` and `ch06:13` open two in a row (nested by accident), `ch06:23` and
  `ch06:98` open without a matching close. `dl open=15 close=11`.
- 3 stray `</p>` (F02) and 1 stray `</figure>`.
- The parser reports the damage at built-HTML lines 1522, 1680, 2003, 2679, 2705, 3007, 3340 — i.e. five distinct
  files once mapped back to `build/content/`.

### Intent
The `.calc` grid aligns `=` signs across rows using shared grid columns. A nested `<dl>` silently re-parents the
`.crow` children into a different grid, so the alignment the CSS promises is *not* the alignment the reader sees —
a defect no linter looks for because the browser repairs the tree. Fix the tree and then make it impossible to
reintroduce, because the generator concatenates 17 hand-written fragments.

### Definition of done
- [ ] `python3 build/check_dom.py` parses the built file with `html.parser` and exits 0; before the fix it must be
      demonstrated to exit 1 with exactly the 7 errors.
- [ ] `dl open == dl close`, `p open == p close`, `figure open == figure close` in the built file.
- [ ] The `#koncentracija` calculation grid is screenshotted before and after; the "=" column must line up in the
      after shot and the reviewer pastes both into the task note.
- [ ] `check_dom.py` is wired into `gate.py` and `check.sh` as step `c_dom` with its own row in `check-report.json`.
- [ ] `check_dom.py` also asserts: no `<p>` inside `<p>`, no block element inside `<summary>`, every `<table>` has
      a caption, every `<svg>` has `viewBox` + `title` + `desc`, every `<img>` has `alt` (currently 0 images —
      the check is a tripwire for future work).

### Task substeps
1. **Baseline the damage.** Write `check_dom.py` first and run it on the *current* file. Record the 7 errors as the
   fixed test vector; the script ships with them as a regression fixture (`build/fixtures/dom_errors.html`).
2. **Repair at source.** Fix the four `dl` blocks in `build/content/ch06.html` and the other three files; never
   patch the generated HTML.
3. **Enforce.** Add the step to both gate runners, and make it fail on any *new* error class it learns about.

### Subtask 2.1 — The checker
- **2.1.a** Implement the stack walker (void-element set for HTML + SVG: `br, hr, img, input, meta, link, source,
  path, rect, circle, use, col, wbr, polyline, line, ellipse, polygon, stop`). Report `(kind, tag, line, column,
  unclosed_stack)` for each error.
- **2.1.b** Add the semantic invariants (caption on table, title+desc on svg, no nested p) as a second pass so the
  step reports two counters: `structure` and `semantics`.
- **2.1.c** Wire a `--json` mode so `check.sh` can store per-error lines in `check-report.json` and the final report
  can quote them verbatim instead of saying "0 problems".

### Subtask 2.2 — The repairs
- **2.2.a** `ch06.html`: delete the duplicated `<dl class="calc">` at line 13, close the first block after B #14's
  last `crow`, and open a fresh `<dl class="calc">` for B #15. The two blocks must stay two `<dl>`s (they are two
  separate worked solutions), each with its own `chead`.
- **2.2.b** Find the other two unclosed `dl`s (parser lines 2679 and 2705) by bisecting with `check_dom.py --file
  build/content/chNN.html`; close them where the calculation ends, not at the end of the chapter.
- **2.2.c** Remove the three stray `</p>` and the stray `</figure>`; for each, decide whether the loose sentence
  belongs to the preceding paragraph (join it) or is a new block (wrap it). Never delete content to make a parser
  happy.

### Subtask 2.3 — Visual proof
- **2.3.a** Screenshot `#koncentracija` and `#stehiometrija` at 1440 px before the fix; store under
  `build/evidence/dom-before-*.png`.
- **2.3.b** Screenshot the same regions after; compare the `=` column x-positions by eye and store as
  `dom-after-*.png`. If the grid still misaligns, the CSS grid is the next suspect — investigate `.calc`'s
  `grid-template-columns` before closing the task.
- **2.3.c** Print those two chapters to PDF and check that no calculation line breaks across pages (print CSS
  already declares `break-inside: avoid` on `.crow`; verify it still applies now that the tree is correct).

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_dom.py --file Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html   # exit 0
python3 build/check_dom.py --fixture                                                 # exit 1 on the 7 known errors
bash build/check.sh                                                                  # c_dom PASS
```

### Guardrails
- Do not switch the whole page to an XML parser or a strict HTML5 validator to "solve" this: the page embeds SVG
  and MathML, and a strict validator will produce hundreds of false positives that no one will triage.
- Do not reformat the content files wholesale. A whitespace-normalising pass would create a diff of thousands of
  lines and destroy reviewability of every later task.

## T03 — Make the quality gate tell the truth

**Theme:** polish out mistakes · process integrity
**Priority:** P0 · **Effort:** S · **Wave:** 1 · **Owner skill:** none (engineering), `audit` for the review ·
**Depends on:** T02 (shares the `check.sh` file)

### Evidence
- `build/check.sh:390` runs inspect with `--allow few-pictures,focal-point,no-footage,still-page`.
- `build/gate.py:172` runs inspect with `--allow few-pictures,focal-point` — a **different** list.
- `build/check-baseline.json` lists `inspect.allowed_fails: ["few-pictures","focal-point"]` — a baseline that
  "allows FAILs", which contradicts the phrase "0 FAIL" printed next to it.
- Raw `inspect.mjs` output this session: `RESULT: 2 FAIL, 6 WARN — not done.`
- The two paragraph-length counters disagree (F22): `deload_report.py` says every chapter has `walls=0`;
  a naive `<p>` split finds 27 over-length paragraphs, most of them figure-caption concatenation.

### Intent
A gate that suppresses what it cannot fix is worse than no gate, because it converts an unknown into a false
certainty, and the final report is built from it. Two things must become true: (a) every suppression is a named,
reasoned **exception** printed in the report; (b) one measurement per claim, so two scripts cannot disagree.

### Definition of done
- [ ] One file, `build/exceptions.json`, holds every suppressed rule:
      `{"rule":"few-pictures","scope":"page","reason":"…","owner":"…","review_by":"…"}`. Both gate runners read it.
      Nothing else may pass `--allow`.
- [ ] `check.sh` and `gate.py` produce **identical** verdicts on the same file; a test asserts it
      (`build/check_gate_parity.py` runs both, compares the step/status rows, exits non-zero on drift).
- [ ] The report line becomes `0 FAIL, N excepted (rule: reason)`, and the final report template
      (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §10.3) is amended to require the exception list.
- [ ] `focal-point` is either genuinely fixed (T04) or excepted with a written design rationale in
      `build/README.md`. The preferred outcome is fixed, because a 214-screen document *can* have a dominant
      first element without becoming a landing page.
- [ ] `few-pictures` is excepted with the reason "a chemistry study text is diagram-led; stock photography of
      laboratories would misrepresent the subject and cannot be sourced offline; all figures are original SVG",
      and the T10–T15 figure programme is cited as the compensating control.
- [ ] The paragraph-length measurement exists in exactly one script (`build/check_text.py`), with a documented
      filter for figure captions; `deload_report.py` imports it instead of reimplementing it.

### Task substeps
1. **Write the exception register.** Turn the two `--allow` lists into one JSON with reasons, and make both
   runners load it.
2. **Unify the measurement.** Extract the sentence/paragraph counter out of `deload_report.py` into a single
   function with explicit exclusions (`figure`, `figcaption`, `dl.calc`, `.defn`), then have both callers use it.
3. **Prove parity.** Add `check_gate_parity.py`, run it, and paste both runners' tables into the task note.

### Subtask 3.1 — Exception register
- **3.1.a** Create `build/exceptions.json` with one entry per currently suppressed rule; every entry needs a
  `reason` of at least one sentence and a `compensating_control` field naming what makes the exception safe.
- **3.1.b** Change `check.sh` to build the `--allow` string from that file instead of hard-coding it, and change
  `gate.py` to do the same; delete the `allowed_fails` block from `check-baseline.json` so the concept "an allowed
  FAIL" no longer exists.
- **3.1.c** Print the register at the top of the gate output and in `--md` mode, so the reader sees exceptions
  before results.

### Subtask 3.2 — One text metric
- **3.2.a** Implement `text_metrics(html)` in `build/check_text.py`: strip `figure`/`figcaption`/`dl` subtrees,
  collapse inline tags, split sentences on `[.!?…]` + capital, return per-paragraph sentence counts, word counts,
  and the list of offenders with their section id.
- **3.2.b** Replace the loop inside `deload_report.py` with `from check_text import text_metrics`; delete the local
  `sents()` so the two numbers cannot drift again.
- **3.2.c** Freeze the current offender list (whatever the honest number is) into `build/text-backlog.json` so T16
  has a work queue and the gate can assert the list shrinks monotonically.

### Subtask 3.3 — Parity test
- **3.3.a** Implement `check_gate_parity.py`: run `bash build/check.sh --md` and `python3 build/gate.py --json`,
  parse both, compare `(step, status)` tuples; exit 1 on any difference, printing the diff.
- **3.3.b** Add the parity test to the gate itself as the last step, so a future edit to one runner cannot land
  without the other.
- **3.3.c** Update `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §9.1 and §10 with the new step numbering and the exception language, and
  note in `build/README.md` why "0 FAIL" was previously not true.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_gate_parity.py            # exit 0, identical verdicts
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('build/exceptions.json'));print(len(d),'exceptions')"
bash build/check.sh --md | head -20
```

### Guardrails
- Do not delete a rule from the inspector, and do not fork the inspector. The exception must stay visible.
- Do not "fix" `few-pictures` by adding stock photography: it would violate `AGENTS.md` §5 (no network, no
  credited images) and misrepresent the subject.
- Do not let `check_gate_parity.py` normalise away timing or ordering differences; compare only `(step, status)`,
  and say so in the script docstring.

## T04 — Masthead: a title plate instead of a landing hero

**Theme:** anti-slop · restyle · first screen
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 2 · **Owner skill:** `design-taste-frontend` (dealt sheet + `lint.mjs`
+ `inspect.mjs`; take the type system and composition only) · **Depends on:** T03 (so the fixed `focal-point` is
judged by an honest gate), T05/T06 (surface and type decisions)

### Evidence
- Current first screen: 5-line kicker ("Medicīniskā ķīmija · Cilvēka fizioloģijas un bioķīmijas katedra · 1. temats"),
  h1 at 54.4 px / 3.8 vw, a two-line standfirst, a three-line meta paragraph, then a boxed contents card with two
  pill buttons. That is the anatomy of a marketing hero (F21).
- `inspect.mjs`: "The first screen has no dominant element: the largest type is 54.4px (3.8vw) and no single
  picture holds a third of the viewport."
- `design-taste-frontend/references/tells.md` bans the kicker/eyebrow, and `AGENTS.md` §6.2 orders the tells
  registry *after* source fidelity and accessibility but *before* study-skill appearance.
- The dark band is `--ink` on `#f6f7f4` with a 20 px visible page margin at the top of the screenshot — the band
  reads as a pasted-on block, not as a page.

### Intent
Replace the hero with a **document title plate**: the object a medical student actually receives — course, topic,
which sources it replaces, what the tier key means, and what changed in this revision. The page's one dominant
element becomes the title itself at display size, set in the document's own type system, with real bibliographic
content under it. No kicker, no pill buttons, no "hero".

### Definition of done
- [ ] The title plate contains, in this order and nothing else: `h1` (≤ 5 words, unchanged text), one line naming
      the course and department, one line naming the five source documents by id (A–E) with page counts, one line
      stating the revision/version, one line explaining the three tier words, and the contents index.
- [ ] No element above the `h1`. The kicker line is deleted, not restyled (record its content in the plate's
      metadata line so no information is lost).
- [ ] The `h1` is the largest type on the page and is set at ≥ 6.5 vw at 1440 px (target: it fills the first
      screen's top third without becoming a poster). `inspect.mjs` `focal-point` passes **without** an exception.
- [ ] Contrast of every plate line measured ≥ 4.5:1 (large type ≥ 3:1) on the composited background; numbers
      pasted in the task note.
- [ ] `lint.mjs` 0 FAIL, and the WARN count does not grow.
- [ ] Print: the plate fits on the first page with the contents index below it, and `@page :first` still suppresses
      the running head (already implemented — verify, don't assume).

### Task substeps
1. **Deal a document direction, not a poster.** Run `draw.mjs` from the scratchpad with the `--avoid` list in
   `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.1; keep only the type system, palette procedure and document-shaped composition. Record
   the direction id in `build/design-brief.md`.
2. **Compose the plate.** Build it as HTML + one authored SVG rule/motif that carries information (see 4.2),
   not as decoration.
3. **Judge it.** Screenshot at 1440/768/390, read the screenshots, remove anything that carries no information.

### Subtask 4.1 — Informational masthead
- **4.1.a** Write `build/design-brief.md` — six lines: idea, type system, palette derivation, chapter opening
  composition, signature move, what is deliberately absent. The idea must come from the subject (notation,
  the pH scale as data, the correction voice), not from a "lab notebook" costume.
- **4.1.b** Rebuild `header.masthead` in `build_master.py` as a `<header>` with a `<h1>`, a `<p class="plate-meta">`
  (course · department · version), a `<ul class="plate-sources">` (A–E with page counts), a `<dl class="plate-tier">`
  (three tier words, defined once), and the contents `<nav>`.
- **4.1.c** Delete the two pill buttons from the plate and relocate their functions to T07's navigation rail
  ("Divu soļu režīms" and "Slēpt atbildes" are document modes, not hero calls-to-action). Keep the same behaviour
  and the same `localStorage` keys so a returning reader's preference survives.

### Subtask 4.2 — The one signature move
- **4.2.a** Choose the move and write it down: **the notation specimen** — a single line of the page's own
  chemistry set at display scale, showing `⇌ → ↑ ↓`, a charge `Fe³⁺`, an oxidation state `(III)`, a formula with
  real subscripts `Al₂(SO₄)₃`, and a decimal comma — the exact things the page promises to get right. It is
  information (it teaches the notation contract in one glance), not ornament.
- **4.2.b** Implement it as one inline SVG with real `<text>` (not an image), `role="img"`, a `<title>`/`<desc>`
  that reads the line aloud, and a print variant that does not rely on colour.
- **4.2.c** Test it in the three fonts the page may actually render in (Inter, Segoe UI, DejaVu Sans) and in print;
  the glyph `⇌` must resolve in all four. If it does not, ship the MathML fallback described in `AGENTS.md` §6.4.

### Subtask 4.3 — Contents index as a real index
- **4.3.a** Replace the 17-item `<ol>` card with a two-column index that carries information: chapter number,
  title, tier words, figure count, question count, and the correction ids that appear in that chapter. Data comes
  from the build, so it cannot drift.
- **4.3.b** Set the index in the same type system as the body (not in buttons or pills), with a filled header row
  and no card background; the page's surface step alone separates it.
- **4.3.c** Verify the print variant shows page numbers (already implemented via `target-counter`) and that the
  numbers are correct in the PDF; screenshot the printed index page.

### Gate
```bash
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lint.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
# expect: focal-point PASS (no exception), 0 FAIL beyond declared exceptions
```

### Guardrails
- Do not add a photograph, an illustration of a laboratory, or a hero image. The document's subject is notation.
- Do not let the plate push the tier key below the fold at 768 px; the exam core must remain reachable from the
  first screen (`AGENTS.md` §4).
- Do not use `100vh` for the plate; a mobile browser's dynamic viewport will clip the contents index.

## T05 — Surface system: retexturing without decoration

**Theme:** retexturing · restyle · anti-slop
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 2 · **Owner skill:** `design-taste-frontend` (`references/colour.md`
procedure; `tufte-margin-scholar` for the margin-rail behaviour only) · **Depends on:** T03

### Evidence
- The page currently has three tonal steps (`--bg #f6f7f4`, `--surface #eaede5`, `--surface-2 #dde2d7`) and one
  border colour `--line #7e887b` used at 3.43:1 — legal for a border, illegal as a text separator if it is ever
  read as one.
- 62 `div.pair` blocks all use the same outlined shape; `inspect.mjs` reports "8 rows of identical boxed cards"
  (F20).
- Callouts are outlined (`div.callout`), and `AGENTS.md` §6.4/`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.6 explicitly bans outlined
  and dashed callout borders: "Callouts are filled tone steps, not outlined or dashed boxes."
- The earlier master's failure list in `AGENTS.md` §6.1 includes "grain overlay", "cream ground with a deep-red
  accent", "3 hairlines", "11 shadows", "13 gradients" — all of which must not come back under the name
  "retexturing".

### Intent
Give the document a **material logic**: four named tone steps with a stated meaning, a plate treatment for
figures and tables, a correction rail that is a surface rather than a border, and one radius decision. "Texture"
here means *tonal and typographic articulation* — how a definition reads differently from a mistake reads
differently from a figure — not paper grain, not noise PNGs, not gradients.

### Definition of done
- [ ] A documented tone scale in `build/assets/style.css` with named tokens and a stated role each:
      `--paper` (page), `--field` (one step in: figure plates, table headers), `--field-2` (two steps in: inline
      code-free formula wells, matrix header), `--rail` (margin rail surface). Max four. Each role written as a
      comment above the token.
- [ ] Every callout, note, mistake block, correction pair and definition uses a **filled tone step + a 3 px
      semantic edge on one side only**, not a full outline and not a dashed border.
- [ ] `grep -c 'border: 1px solid'` in the stylesheet drops to the count needed for genuine data tables only, and
      that count is recorded. `border-dashed` count = 0 outside figure construction lines.
- [ ] One radius decision, applied everywhere: `--radius: 0` **or** `--radius: 999px` (fully round), never a mix.
      Recommendation: square, because the page contains 41 tables and rounded table corners fight every one.
- [ ] No gradient, no `box-shadow` at rest, no `backdrop-filter`, no `background-image` texture. Assert with grep
      and paste the command output.
- [ ] Contrast re-measured for every text-on-tone pair after the change; a table of pairs and ratios in the task
      note. Nothing below 4.5:1 for text below 24 px.
- [ ] Print: the four tones collapse to two ink-safe steps (white + one 8 % grey) and `print-color-adjust: exact`
      is only used where a swatch is *data* (the pH strip).

### Task substeps
1. **Derive the scale.** Take the existing palette and formalise it; do not add a new hue. Measure each step's
   contrast against the text colour and against each other, and keep only the steps that survive.
2. **Apply roles.** Rewrite `.defn`, `.mist`, `.pair`, `.note`, `.callout`, `figure`, `table.data`, `table.mx` to
   use the four tokens and one edge rule.
3. **Sweep and prove.** Grep for banned treatments, re-measure contrast, screenshot a representative 12-screen
   stretch, and read it.

### Subtask 5.1 — Tone scale and role map
- **5.1.a** Write the role map as a comment block at the top of the CSS: *paper* = reading ground; *field* =
  "this block is a different kind of thing" (figure plate, table head); *field-2* = "this block is nested inside
  one" (matrix header inside a table section); *rail* = "this text sits beside the argument, not in it"
  (corrections, definitions).
- **5.1.b** Reduce to four steps by measuring: keep `--bg`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, and add `--rail` only if
  it differs from `--surface` by ≥ 4 ΔL* (otherwise reuse `--surface` and say so). Any step that does not earn a
  role is deleted, not kept "for variety".
- **5.1.c** Re-derive the three semantic colours so that each is defined once as a *pair* (`--def` / `--def-field`)
  and is always accompanied by a text label, never colour alone (`AGENTS.md` §6.2, cognitive-deload gate).

### Subtask 5.2 — Component surfaces
- **5.2.a** `.defn`: convert from an outlined box to a filled `--def-field` block with a 3 px `--def` left edge and
  the "Definīcija" tag inline as the first words (not a separate badge). Measure the contrast of the tag against
  the field.
- **5.2.b** `.pair` (the 62 correction pairs): drop the box entirely on wide screens and give it a rail surface
  with a top rule only; under 900 px it becomes an inline `<details>` whose summary is the source's own phrase.
  Keep the `Avotā / Pareizi / Kāpēc` order and the id.
- **5.2.c** `figure`: replace the current flat `--bg` fill with a `--field` plate that has an inner padding of one
  line-height, a caption above the drawing set in small caps-free small text, and a 1 px top rule. The plate is
  the only place a border is allowed besides tables.

### Subtask 5.3 — Texture sweep and evidence
- **5.3.a** Grep audit: `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, `linear-gradient`, `radial-gradient`, `backdrop-filter`,
  `border-dashed`, `background-image`, `opacity: 0.` (the last one catches faded text like F12). Record counts
  before/after.
- **5.3.b** Recompute the WCAG matrix for every new pair with the same script used in this inspection
  (`build/deload_report.py` already has `ratio()`); paste the table.
- **5.3.c** Screenshot a 12-screen vertical slice covering a chapter opening, a correction pair, a table, a
  figure and a mistake block at 1440 and 390; read them and delete one thing that turns out to be decoration.

### Gate
```bash
grep -cE 'gradient|box-shadow|backdrop-filter|border-dashed' build/assets/style.css   # 0
python3 build/deload_report.py | head -12                                             # contrast table
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lint.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html
```

### Guardrails
- "Texture" must never mean a raster noise overlay. That is exactly the earlier master's failure (`AGENTS.md`
  §6.1) and would fail the lint.
- Do not remove the three semantic colours to "reduce" them: the rule is ≤ 3 semantic colours, each with a role
  and a doubled text label — not zero.
- Do not use the pH scale's indicator colours as a page accent. They are data, confined to that one figure
  (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.4 exception).

## T06 — Type system, figure typography and portability

**Theme:** restyle · typography · correctness of rendering
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 2 · **Owner skill:** `impeccable` (`typeset` reference),
`design-taste-frontend` (`references/type.md`) · **Depends on:** T03

### Evidence
- `inspect.mjs`: sizes in use are **9 / 12 / 13 / 17 / 18 / 30 / 54 px**, body 17 px / 1.55 — seven sizes, several
  a single pixel apart. `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.5 asks for "Five type sizes, far apart".
- Inside SVG, `.lbl`, `.lbl.sm`, `.lbl.xs`, `.z`, `.ren` are all 13 px (F10), plus inline `font-size="12"` and
  `font-size="20"` overrides in two figures.
- `--font-text: "Inter", "Segoe UI", "DejaVu Sans", "Noto Sans", system-ui` — Inter is installed *here*
  (`fc-match Inter` → `Inter-Regular.ttf`) but not embedded, so the file renders differently on any machine
  without it (F23). `inspect.mjs` warns `font-fallback` for `DejaVu Sans, math`.
- `--font-sym` ends with `Noto Sans Math`, which is declared but not shipped; the `⇌` (U+21CC) glyph is
  load-bearing for the chemistry notation contract.
- The 9 px size appears once, in print CSS; the 12 px appears in figure overrides. Neither is part of a scale.

### Intent
Five sizes, far apart, one family decision that is **portable offline**, and a *real* type scale inside SVG that
survives being scaled down. The reader should be able to print the file, open it on a Windows laptop and on a
phone, and get the same hierarchy every time.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Exactly five text sizes, defined once as `--t-1 … --t-5`, with a stated ratio (recommended ≈ 1.33) and a
      stated use for each. No other `font-size` value exists in the stylesheet except SVG artwork constants and
      the print block.
- [ ] A font decision, written down with its licence and size consequence, choosing exactly one of:
      **(a)** embed a subset `woff2` (Inter is SIL OFL; subset Latin + Latin-Extended + the chemistry glyphs
      `Δαρσπ·²³⁺⁻₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉⇌→↑↓−`) and pay the bytes; **(b)** ship a system stack and delete "Inter" from the CSS
      so screenshots are honest. If (a), the total size budget must be re-derived and `check_size.py` updated.
- [ ] A **glyph proof** page (`build/font-proof.html` refreshed) rendered in the final font at 3 sizes, showing
      `āčēģīķļņšūž ĀČĒĢĪĶĻŅŠŪŽ Δαρσπ · ² ³ ⁺ ⁻ ₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉ ⇌ → ↑ ↓ − „ “`; screenshot attached.
- [ ] SVG typography uses three sizes only: `--fig-1` (data/axis labels), `--fig-2` (annotations), `--fig-3`
      (headline inside a figure), with a hard floor of 12 user units at a 760-unit canvas. No inline
      `font-size=` attributes remain.
- [ ] `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` applies to `table.data`, `table.mx`, `.calc`, the glossary symbol
      column and **all** SVG numeric labels; proportional lining figures for prose.
- [ ] Print sizes re-derived from the same scale (10.5 pt body is currently set independently and conflicts with
      the screen scale's 17 px).

### Task substeps
1. **Audit and choose.** Inventory every size, every family and every numeric figure setting; decide (a) or (b);
   measure the byte cost if (a).
2. **Implement the scale.** Replace all ad-hoc sizes with the five tokens; fix SVG sizes; make numerics
   consistent.
3. **Prove rendering.** Glyph proof, screenshot in the real font, print proof, and a size-budget check.

### Subtask 6.1 — Family and glyphs
- **6.1.a** Build the glyph inventory from the page itself: extract every distinct codepoint, list the non-ASCII
  ones, and check the chosen font covers all of them. Do this with a script (`build/glyphs.py`), not by eye.
- **6.1.b** If embedding: subset with `pyftsubset`/`fonttools` to `latin,latin-ext` + the explicit glyph list,
  base64 into the CSS, add the OFL notice in the appendix, and record the added KB.
- **6.1.c** If the system stack: remove "Inter" and "Noto Sans Math" from every stack, add a documented fallback
  chain that ends in `sans-serif`, and confirm `⇌` still resolves — if not, implement the MathML/SVG fallback for
  that single glyph as `AGENTS.md` §6.4 allows.

### Subtask 6.2 — The five-size scale
- **6.2.a** Define `--t-1` (small/caption), `--t-2` (secondary/annotations), `--t-3` (body), `--t-4` (chapter
  headings), `--t-5` (page title), with a ratio table and the px/vw behaviour at 390/768/1440.
- **6.2.b** Map every existing class to one token and delete the rest. The 13 px `.small`, the 12 px SVG override
  and the 9 px print size must each be resolved by moving to the nearest token or by adding a print-only token with
  a documented reason.
- **6.2.c** Re-run `inspect.mjs` and assert the "sizes in use" line reports exactly five values (plus print-only
  ones, which the inspector does not see).

### Subtask 6.3 — Figure type and numerics
- **6.3.a** Replace the five 13 px SVG classes with the three-token figure scale; fold `.lbl.xs` into `.lbl`
  (they are currently identical, so the distinction is a lie) and give the remaining two a real size difference.
- **6.3.b** Set `tabular-nums` on all SVG `<text>` that contains digits, and add `font-feature-settings: "lnum"`
  where lining figures are needed inside a figure.
- **6.3.c** Print-proof one figure per type size at 100 %: no label may fall below 7.5 pt on A4 at 16 mm margins;
  if it does, the figure gets a print variant (deferred to T12) or fewer labels.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/glyphs.py                       # every codepoint covered
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
grep -c 'font-size:' build/assets/style.css   # ≤ 12 (five tokens + print + outliers with comments)
python3 build/check_size.py
```

### Guardrails
- Do not set type below 13 px for anything a reader must read; 9 px exists only in print CSS and should not survive.
- Do not use monospace for "technical" labels (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.5 forbids it).
- If the font is embedded, `AGENTS.md` §8's no-network rule still holds: `data:` URIs only, no `<link>`.

## T07 — Navigation, progress and a way back

**Theme:** functionality · wayfinding · accessibility
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 3 · **Owner skill:** `tufte-margin-scholar` (rail mechanics),
`audit` (focus order) · **Depends on:** T04 (the contents index moves), T05 (rail surface)

### Evidence
- 214.5 screens tall, 55 sections, 442 links, and **no** persistent navigation: no chapter rail, no scroll-spy,
  no "back to contents", no skip link (F15).
- The only contents list is a card at the very top; after the first screen it is unreachable without 214 screens
  of scrolling.
- Keyboard: 1,326 interactive nodes in reading order, and no way to jump a chapter or skip the navigation.
- The page already has stable ids for every section (440 anchors, 384 ids, 0 heading skips per `c_anchors`), so the
  data for navigation exists; only the UI is missing.

### Intent
A reader should always know three things: where they are, what else exists, and how to get back. This is the
single biggest usability gain available, and it is entirely client-side, offline, and degradable.

### Definition of done
- [ ] A **skip link** is the first focusable element: *"Pāriet uz saturu"* → `#main`, visible on focus.
- [ ] A **chapter rail** at ≥ 1100 px: 17 entries, current chapter marked by tone + `aria-current="true"`, each
      showing tier words; sticky, max height 100 vh minus header, scrollable on its own, never overlapping the
      reading column.
- [ ] Under 1100 px the rail becomes a top sheet: a `<details>` "Nodaļas" that opens to the same 17 entries,
      keyboard-operable, closes on `Esc`.
- [ ] **Reading progress** expressed in content, not decoration: "Nodaļa 8 no 17 · 46 %" in the rail, updated on
      scroll with `IntersectionObserver`, `aria-live="polite"` but throttled so it does not spam a screen reader.
- [ ] A **"uz saturu"** control appears in the rail only after the second screen and returns to `#saturs`.
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts, documented in the plate: `g` then `t` (contents), `n`/`p` (next/previous chapter),
      `s` (search, once T09 lands), `?` (shortcut list). All disabled while focus is in an input/textarea, and all
      listed in a `<details>` "Tastatūras īsinājumi".
- [ ] JS off: the rail, progress and shortcuts are absent, the contents index at the top still works, and no
      navigation is *required* to read the page (verify by disabling JS and completing a chapter).
- [ ] Print: no rail, no progress, no skip link; contents page numbers still correct.

### Task substeps
1. **Structure the navigation data.** Derive the chapter list from the build (id, title, tier, figure count,
   question count), not from a hand-typed array, so it cannot drift.
2. **Build the rail and the sheet.** One data source, two presentations, one keyboard model.
3. **Add progress and shortcuts**, then tab through the whole page and record the focus order.

### Subtask 7.1 — Navigation model
- **7.1.a** Add `build/nav.py` (or extend `prereq.py`) that emits `build/nav.json`: for each chapter, `id`, `n`,
  `title`, `tier_words`, `figure_count`, `question_count`, `correction_ids`, `word_count`. The plate index (T04)
  and the rail both read this file.
- **7.1.b** Render the rail from `nav.json` in `build_master.py` as a `<nav aria-label="Nodaļas">` with an `<ol>`,
  each `<li>` containing one `<a href="#id">` with a `<span class="num">` (tabular) and the title; the tier words
  as plain text, not a badge.
- **7.1.c** Mark the current item with `aria-current="true"` and a tone change, and add `scroll-margin-top` to
  every section so a jump does not hide the heading under a sticky bar.

### Subtask 7.2 — Mobile sheet and focus order
- **7.2.a** Wrap the rail in `<details class="rail-sheet">` under 1100 px with `<summary>Nodaļas</summary>`; the
  same `<ol>` is reused (one DOM, not two), so there is no content duplication and no "hidden duplicate link"
  accessibility trap.
- **7.2.b** Implement `Esc` to close, focus return to the summary, and `aria-expanded` maintained by JS (with the
  native `<details>` behaviour as the no-JS fallback).
- **7.2.c** Tab through the page from the top and write down the first 25 stops; the skip link must be first, the
  rail second, the plate third. Fix any focusable element that is visually hidden but tabbable.

### Subtask 7.3 — Progress, shortcuts, and the way back
- **7.3.a** Implement progress with `IntersectionObserver` over `<section class="chapter">`, updating a single
  `aria-live` node with a throttled (≥ 1 s) message; store nothing in `localStorage` unless the reader opts in.
- **7.3.b** Implement the shortcut map with a single `keydown` handler, an ignore-list for `input|textarea|select|
  [contenteditable]`, and a `?` overlay that is a `<dialog>` with focus trap and `Esc`.
- **7.3.c** Add the "uz saturu" control and make sure it does not appear over a figure or a table on any
  breakpoint; verify at 1440/1100/768/390.

```bash
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
```

Plus a manual record: 25-tab focus list pasted in the task note, and a JS-off screenshot of the rail area.

### Guardrails
- No hamburger icon, no emoji, no icon-only control. Text labels only (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §7.6).

## T08 — Control density, button hierarchy and microcopy

**Theme:** functionality · restyle · cognitive load
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 3 · **Owner skill:** `cognitive-deload-auditor`,
`design-taste-frontend` (`references/tells.md` for the button/pill rules) · **Depends on:** T05, T07

### Evidence
- 1,326 interactive nodes: 357 `<button>`, 215 `<input>`, 442 `<a>`, 312 `<summary>` (F14).
- 19 figures × 4 toolbar buttons = 76 buttons that all read as equally important ("Rādīt apzīmējumus", "Slēpt
  apzīmējumus", "Pārbaude", "Rādīt nākamo"), plus a `fig-status` live region per figure.
- 195 elements use `class="btn secondary"` — one visual weight for almost everything.
- 53 `.btn-print-ch` occurrences (51 controls, one per chapter and per check block, plus 2 CSS references).
- The tiles registry bans pill badges and icon-in-rounded-square; the current buttons are small filled rectangles,
  which is acceptable, but their *count and parity* is the problem, not their shape.

### Intent
Reduce the number of decisions the reader must make per screen. A figure is something to look at; studying it is
a mode you enter on purpose, once, with a clear entry and exit. A page-level tool belongs in a page-level place.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Each figure has **one** control: `<summary>Pētīt attēlu</summary>` (a `<details>`), which reveals the study
      modes (mask / review / next), the status line, and a "beigt" control. Total figure buttons drop from 76 to
      ≤ 19 (one summary each) plus in-mode controls that exist only while the mode is open.
- [ ] The three page modes (two-pass, hide answers, print chapter) live in one page-level tools element, not in 51
      per-chapter buttons; per-chapter print moves into a single `Izdrukāt` menu listing chapters.
- [ ] At most **three** button weights exist: primary (one per view), secondary (default), quiet (inline text
      control). `class="btn secondary"` count drops by ≥ 60 %; the exact before/after count is recorded.
- [ ] Every control's accessible name states its effect and its object: "Rādīt atbildi: cik jonu dod
      Al₂(SO₄)₃", not "nē" (this overlaps T19 and must be done once, here, for the 22 inline buttons too).
- [ ] No control is reachable only by hover; all targets ≥ 44 × 44 px at 390 px; focus ring ≥ 3:1 against both the
      control and the page.
- [ ] A "control census" script (`build/check_controls.py`) reports counts by class, by chapter and by accessible
      name length; it runs in the gate so density cannot creep back.

### Task substeps
1. **Census.** Count every control by type, class, chapter and accessible name; find the ones that do the same
   thing in different places.
2. **Consolidate.** One figure disclosure, one page tools element, three weights, meaningful names.
3. **Re-test.** Keyboard, tap size, JS-off behaviour, print.

### Subtask 8.1 — Census and naming
- **8.1.a** Write `build/check_controls.py` that walks the built DOM and emits a table: `class`, `count`,
  `chapters`, `min accessible name length`, `max`, plus a list of names under 4 characters.
- **8.1.b** Classify the 357 buttons into ≤ 8 *jobs* (answer reveal, figure study, page mode, chapter print, quiz
  option, quiz check, matrix mask, scrubber step) and map every class to exactly one job.
- **8.1.c** Fix the 22 one-word reveal buttons (F17): give each an `aria-label` built from its own question text
  via the build (the data is already there in the quiz/question model), keeping the visible word unchanged.

### Subtask 8.2 — Figure study mode
- **8.2.a** Convert every `figure[data-occ]` toolbar into a `<details class="fig-study">` whose summary is
  "Pētīt attēlu"; move the four controls and the status inside; the controls render only when open (`.live`
  pattern already used by the scrubbers — reuse it).
- **8.2.b** Keep the occlusion behaviour identical (show / mask / review / next) but make the mask state persist
  across a resize and be announced once, not per label.
- **8.2.c** Ensure the static, no-JS and print states show the figure fully labelled — a study mode must never be
  the only way to read the drawing.

### Subtask 8.3 — Page tools and weights
- **8.3.a** Build one `<div class="doc-tools">` in the plate/rail area with: two-pass mode, hide answers, print

- **8.3.b** Reduce the CSS to `--btn-primary`, `--btn-secondary`, `--btn-quiet`; delete the rest; verify no view
  has more than one primary action.
- **8.3.c** Re-run the census and screenshot every distinct control state (rest / hover / focus / open / disabled)
  into the evidence folder; read them as a set to confirm they look like one family.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_controls.py            # ≤ 8 jobs, 0 names < 4 chars, targets ≥ 44 px
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lint.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html
```

### Guardrails
- Do not hide required content behind a study mode. Everything in a figure must be readable with JS off.

## T09 — Offline search over the whole material

**Theme:** functionality · addon feature
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 3 · **Owner skill:** none (engineering); `cognitive-deload-auditor`
for the result design · **Depends on:** T01 (terms are stable), T02 (DOM parsing), T07 (a place to put it)

### Evidence
- The material is 30,979 words and is explicitly meant to be "looked up in afterwards"
  (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §1). There is no search of any kind (F16).
- The page is one file with zero network, so search must be a **build-time index** plus client-side matching, not
  a service.
- 440 anchors and 384 ids exist, so every result can deep-link to an exact place.
- The glossary already has a filter input (`#gloss-filter`), which proves the interaction pattern is acceptable
  in this document.

### Intent
Type "šķīdība", get: the definition, the chapter, the figure, the correction that concerns it, and the glossary
row. Type "6,88" and get the worked problem that produces it. Search is the highest-value feature this document
can gain and it costs no bytes until it is opened.

### Definition of done
- [ ] `build/build_index.py` emits a compact JSON index at build time: `{id, kind, title, text, chapter, tier,
      anchors}` for each searchable unit — chapter titles, `h3` headings, `.defn` definitions, `.mist` items,
      correction pairs (by id and by phrase), glossary rows, worked-problem titles, quiz prompts (prompt only,
      never the answer), figure captions and figure titles.
- [ ] The index is embedded as `<script type="application/json" id="search-index">` with `<` escaped, and is
      **not** inlined into JS source (keeps the JS budget).
- [ ] UI: a search field in the rail/plate, keyboard `s` or `/`, results as a list of ≤ 20 matches with the matched
      term highlighted, the chapter, the kind ("definīcija", "labojums", "attēls", "uzdevums", "jautājums") and a
      deep link. Announcement via `aria-live`, full keyboard operation, `Esc` to close.
- [ ] Matching rules are documented: case- and diacritic-insensitive (ā→a), whole-word boost, prefix match, and
      a hard cap. Latvian diacritics must not require the reader to type them.
- [ ] JS off: a static **"Meklētājs"** section in ch17 rendering the same index as an alphabetical `<details>` list
      grouped by chapter — the feature degrades to an index, not to a dead control (and the control is absent, not
      disabled).
- [ ] Index size measured and reported; if > 120 KB uncompressed, trim to headings + definitions + corrections and
      say what was dropped.
- [ ] Search never returns an answer that was supposed to be hidden: a quiz result links to the question, not the
      explanation.

### Task substeps
1. **Build the index.** Decide searchable units, extract them from the model (not by scraping the built page),
   normalise diacritics at match time, not at index time.
2. **Build the UI.** One input, one result list, one keyboard model, one live region, one static fallback.
3. **Test.** Latvian queries with and without diacritics, formula queries (`Al2(SO4)3` typed plainly), a number
   query, a nonsense query, a 1-character query, and a 200 ms debounce budget.

### Subtask 9.1 — Index
- **9.1.a** Extend `build_master.py` to collect units as it assembles chapters (it already walks `ledger.py`,
  `glossary.py`, `quiz.py`), writing `build/search-index.json` with a stable `anchor` per unit.
- **9.1.b** Normalise: strip Latvian diacritics, lowercase, collapse whitespace; keep the original string for
  display so highlighting shows the real spelling. Store a `kind` and a `chapter` for grouping.
- **9.1.c** Add `build/check_index.py` asserting: every anchor exists in the page, no duplicate anchors, no
  answer text in the index, and the index rebuilds byte-identically from the same content (determinism).

### Subtask 9.2 — Interface
- **9.2.a** Markup: `<form role="search">` with a labelled input, a `<ul role="listbox">` of results (or a plain
  list with links — simpler and more robust), a `<p aria-live="polite">` count line, and a "notīrīt" quiet button.
- **9.2.b** Behaviour: debounce 150 ms, `String.prototype.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{Diacritic}/gu,'')` for both
  sides, rank title > definition > body, cap at 20, `↑/↓` to move, `Enter` to open, `Esc` to close, focus returns
  to the trigger.
- **9.2.c** Visual: results as a plain list with the matched substring in a `--def` tone and no card boxes; each
  row shows `<span class="kind">labojums</span> E22 · 5. nodaļa · Šķīdība un temperatura`.

### Subtask 9.3 — Static fallback and measurement
- **9.3.a** Render the full index in ch17 as `<details><summary>Alfabētisks rādītājs</summary>` grouped by chapter,
  with each entry a link; this is the no-JS answer and also a printable index.
- **9.3.b** Budget the index: measure gzip-equivalent size (the file is uncompressed on disk, so measure raw and
  state it), and decide whether to keep captions in the index.
- **9.3.c** Write a tiny, dependency-free test harness (`build/test_search.mjs`, node) that loads the index JSON
  and asserts 12 query→expected-anchor pairs; run it in the gate.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/build_index.py && python3 build/check_index.py
node build/test_search.mjs                       # 12 query→anchor assertions
node -e "const s=require('fs').statSync('build/search-index.json');console.log(s.size)"
```

### Guardrails
- No fuzzy library, no `fetch`, no worker that loads a second file. One JSON blob inside the page.
- Do not index the answer text of any `details.answer`, and do not index `[jāpārbauda]` notes out of context.
- Do not make search the only way to find a section; T04's index and the rail remain primary.

## T10 — The SVG standard: type, colour, labels, data, a11y

**Theme:** more correct SVG · restyle · correctness
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 4 · **Owner skill:** `svg-spatial-occlusion` (behaviour),
`impeccable` (`typeset` for in-figure type), `design-taste-frontend` (`references/type.md`) · **Depends on:** T05
(surfaces), T06 (type scale)

### Evidence
- 16 SVGs, all drawn to a 760-unit canvas (the DAG to 560), all sharing one flat CSS block.
- The figure type scale is fake: five classes at 13 px (F10); one figure overrides with `font-size="12"` and another
  with `font-size="20"` inline.
- Hard-coded colours in figures (`#c9604f`, `#d9e1e6`, `#fff`) bypass the token system and fail contrast: white on
  `#c9604f` = 3.99:1 at 13 px (F11).
- Spectator ions are faded with `opacity="0.45"`, taking 12 px text under AA (F12).
- Sub/superscripts inside SVG use `baseline-shift` + `font-size="0.72em"` in 9 places; `baseline-shift` is
  deprecated in SVG 2 and its support varies in print engines.
- Some labels are placed by absolute coordinates with hand-tuned offsets (`dy=-34`, `+40`), which is how collisions
  happen when a label grows.
- Every figure does have `role="img"`, `<title>` and `<desc>` — that part is good and must be kept.

### Intent
One written standard, applied to every existing figure, so the diagrams look like one draughtsman drew them and so
that a new figure (T13–T15) has a specification to be checked against rather than a vibe. "More correct SVG" has
three meanings here: **scientifically correct data**, **typographically correct labels**, **accessibly correct
implementation**.

### Definition of done
- [ ] `build/SVG_STANDARD.md` exists, is ≤ 120 lines, and is normative (must/should/may), covering: canvas and
      margins; one grid unit; three type tokens with a 12-unit floor; colour tokens only (zero hex); stroke
      hierarchy (three widths, no more); label placement (outside the drawing, straight leaders, never over a
      shape); collision rule; number formatting (decimal comma, thin no-break space); arrowheads; state symbols;
      `title`/`desc` content rules; print; mobile; data provenance.
- [ ] Zero hard-coded colours in `figures.py`; every fill/stroke uses a CSS custom property that is itself defined
      for screen, print and high-contrast modes.
- [ ] Zero inline `font-size`/`opacity`/`fill` attributes in figure markup; all styling in classes.
- [ ] Zero `baseline-shift`; sub/superscripts use explicit `dy` + `font-size` `<tspan>` (or `<tspan class="sub">`
      with CSS `baseline-shift` as a *progressive* enhancement, with the dy fallback present).
- [ ] Every numeric label in every figure is produced by a constant that `check_numbers.py` asserts (solubility
      points, ΔREN values, pH values, REN table). No figure may carry a number that exists only in `figures.py`.
- [ ] `svg .lbl` and descendants have three distinct sizes; a measurement table of each figure's smallest label in
      rendered px at 1440/768/390 is attached.
- [ ] Contrast: every text-on-shape pair in every figure ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for ≥ 24 px); the faded-spectator technique
      is replaced by a dashed outline or a text label "skatītājjons", not by opacity.
- [ ] Print: no figure relies on a fill lighter than 10 % grey for meaning; hatch patterns (SVG `<pattern>`) used
      where two hues would otherwise be the only distinction.

### Task substeps
1. **Write the standard** from the existing 16 figures: what they already do right, what varies, what is
   inconsistent. Make the rules enforceable by a script where possible.
2. **Refactor the CSS + `figures.py`** to the standard; keep every drawing's geometry, change only its expression.
3. **Prove** with an automated audit (T11) plus a visual contact sheet of all 16 figures at three widths.

### Subtask 10.1 — Geometry and type
- **10.1.a** Fix the canvas convention: 760 × N with a 40-unit margin, one 20-unit baseline grid, and a documented
      safe area; the DAG (560 × 618) is the exception and gets its own note.
- **10.1.b** Replace the five 13 px classes with `--fig-1/2/3` and a documented use for each; set a hard floor of
      12 user units and add `text-rendering: geometricPrecision`.
- **10.1.c** Move all labels off the drawing: labels sit in reserved bands (left/right/top/bottom), connections are
      straight `<path class="leader">` segments with a 6-unit gap before the shape, and no leader crosses another
      leader. For each figure, note in `figures.py` which band each label belongs to.

### Subtask 10.2 — Colour and strokes
- **10.2.a** Define figure tokens in the stylesheet: `--fig-ink`, `--fig-muted`, `--fig-field`, `--fig-pos`,
      `--fig-neg`, `--fig-data-1`, `--fig-data-2`, `--fig-alert`, each with screen + print values. Delete every hex
      from `figures.py`.
- **10.2.b** Set a three-level stroke hierarchy: structural (2 px), leader/axis (1 px), emphasis (2.5 px), all via
      classes; arrowheads are shared `<marker>` definitions rather than per-figure triangle paths (currently 8
      hand-drawn arrowheads repeat `l-8 -4 v8 z`, which drifts).
- **10.2.c** Replace `opacity` fades with a semantic treatment: a dashed outline + a legend row "izsvītrots =
      skatītājjons" (visible, printable, contrast-safe). Re-measure every pair and paste the table.

### Subtask 10.3 — Data provenance and accessibility
- **10.3.a** Move every figure constant into `build/figdata.py` (or a section of `figures.py` marked `DATA`), and
      make `check_numbers.py` import and assert it: solubility points (34/35, 64/75, 80/88), ΔREN (0,35 … 3,00),
      pH colours count = 15, dispersion boundaries, the 22 DAG edges, REN table values.
- **10.3.b** Rewrite all 16 `<desc>` elements to state *what to notice*, not what is drawn: "NaCl līkne ir gandrīz
      plakana, tāpēc temperatūra to gandrīz neietekmē" rather than "three curves are shown". Keep the existing
      Latvian voice.
- **10.3.c** Add a visible `<figcaption>` "ko ievērot" line to every figure (most have one — normalise the shape)
      and make the figure's `aria-describedby` point at both `<desc>` and the caption's key sentence.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_numbers.py                  # includes figure data
grep -cE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}' build/figures.py   # 0
grep -c 'font-size=' build/figures.py           # 0
grep -c 'baseline-shift' build/figures.py       # 0
```

### Guardrails
- Do not redraw a figure for beauty. Geometry changes only where a rule is broken or a label collides.
- Do not add a legend to a figure that needs none; the rule is "legend only when a mark is not self-evident".
- Keep every figure's `<title>` id unique; 16 figures × 2 ids is a duplicate-id trap the build currently avoids.

## T11 — Automated SVG audit (the enforcement for T10)

**Theme:** more correct SVG · tooling · quality gate
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 4 · **Owner skill:** none (engineering; reuse
`design-taste-frontend/scripts/lib/cdp.mjs` to drive Chrome) · **Depends on:** T10 (the standard), T03 (the gate)

### Evidence
- Nothing in the current gate measures a figure. `check_components.py` checks scrubber structure;
  `inspect.mjs` only counts pictures. A label can sit on top of another label and every gate stays green.
- The figures use hand-placed coordinates with `dy` offsets, which is exactly the pattern that produces collisions
  when text length changes with the font.
- The page already ships the machinery needed: `lib/cdp.mjs` drives the installed Chrome with zero dependencies.

### Intent
Turn the SVG standard into a test. For each SVG, render it in Chrome, take every `<text>` node's `getBBox()`, and
fail the build on: text overlapping text, text outside the viewBox, text under 12 units, text over a filled shape
without contrast, and leaders crossing text. This is cheap, deterministic, and it is the only way 16 existing plus
18 new figures stay correct as they are edited.

### Definition of done
- [ ] `build/check_svg.py` (or `.mjs`) exists, takes the built HTML, extracts each `<svg>`, renders it in a
      headless page at a fixed width, and returns per-figure findings as JSON.
- [ ] Checks implemented, each with a named rule id:
      `svg-text-overlap` (bbox intersection > 12 % of the smaller box), `svg-overflow` (bbox outside viewBox by
      > 1 unit), `svg-min-font` (< 12 user units), `svg-empty-label` (< 3 chars), `svg-dup-id`,
      `svg-missing-desc`, `svg-hex-fill` (any literal hex in `fill`/`stroke`), `svg-leader-cross`
      (leader path intersecting a text bbox), `svg-contrast` (text fill vs nearest background shape < 4.5).
- [ ] Baseline: all 16 existing figures are audited and the current findings are recorded in
      `build/svg-baseline.json`; the gate fails on **new** findings and on any baseline entry that is not fixed by
      the end of the wave (the baseline is a to-do list with an expiry, not a permanent excuse).
- [ ] The audit runs in `check.sh` and `gate.py` as step `c_svg` and takes < 20 s.
- [ ] A contact sheet (`build/evidence/svg-contact-{1440,768,390}.png`) is generated automatically — one image with
      all figures, so a human can see them as a set.

### Task substeps
1. **Extract and render.** Get each `<svg>` out of the page with its CSS, into a minimal harness page.
2. **Measure.** Implement the nine rules against `getBBox()` and computed styles.
3. **Baseline, then tighten.** Record current state, wire into the gate, and schedule the fixes into T10's sweep.

### Subtask 11.1 — Harness
- **11.1.a** Write a node script using `lib/cdp.mjs`: start Chrome headless, load the built page, evaluate a
      function that returns `[{index, id, title, viewBox, texts:[{x,y,w,h,text,size,fill}]}]` for all SVGs.
- **11.1.b** Attach the page's own stylesheet to the extracted SVG (inject the `<style>` into the harness) so the
      computed font size is the real one, not a default.
- **11.1.c** Cache by content hash so the gate stays fast; invalidate when `figures.py` or the CSS changes.

### Subtask 11.2 — Rules
- **11.2.a** Implement the geometry rules (overlap, overflow, min-font, empty-label) first — they are pure maths on
      bboxes and have almost no false positives.
- **11.2.b** Implement the style rules (hex-fill, missing-desc, duplicate id) by reading the markup, not the
      rendered tree, so they work even if the harness fails.
- **11.2.c** Implement the two hard rules last (leader-cross, contrast) with a documented tolerance; if a rule is
      too noisy, keep it as a WARN with a threshold and say why in the script docstring rather than deleting it.

### Subtask 11.3 — Baseline and gate
- **11.3.a** Run against the current page, triage every finding into `build/svg-baseline.json` with
      `{figure, rule, reason, fix_task}`.
- **11.3.b** Wire into both gate runners with the same exception mechanism as T03 (so an accepted finding is an
      exception with a reason, not a silenced rule).
- **11.3.c** Generate the contact sheet and add it to the T10/T12 review checklist; a human still has to look.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_svg.py --file Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --json
# exit 0 with 0 NEW findings; baseline count printed
bash build/check.sh | grep c_svg
```

### Guardrails
- Do not "fix" a collision by shrinking the font. The rule exists to prevent exactly that.
- Do not tune the overlap threshold until the build passes. Fix the drawing or record an exception.
- The harness must work offline and with the same Chrome the inspector uses; no npm install.

## T12 — Figure legibility on a phone and on paper

**Theme:** more correct SVG · responsive · print
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 4 · **Owner skill:** `print-css-alchemist`, `break-ui` (stress at
390 px), `svg-spatial-occlusion` (tap behaviour) · **Depends on:** T10, T11

### Evidence
- `figure svg { width: 100%; height: auto }` with no minimum width. At a 390 px viewport the reading column is
  ≈ 356 px, so a 760-unit canvas renders at **0.468 scale**. A 13 px label becomes ≈ **6.1 px** (F09). The mobile
  screenshot confirms labels are unreadable in `fig-lattice` and `fig-solvation`.
- 3 rows still scroll sideways at 390 px with content past the edge, with no affordance (F19).
- Print: A4 at 16 mm margins gives ≈ 178 mm for the reading column; a 760-unit canvas prints at ≈ 94 % — labels
  are fine on paper. The problem is screen-only, and it is worst exactly where a student revises: on a phone.
- The figures carry 4 controls each; on a phone those controls stack above the drawing and push it below the fold.

### Intent
A phone is a legitimate revision device. A figure must be readable at 390 px without pinch-zoom, or it must
honestly become a different composition — not a shrunken poster. Paper must get its own scale, and tables must
scroll with an affordance rather than clip.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Every figure declares a **minimum legible width** (in px, derived from its smallest label: `min_px =
      12 / smallest_font_units * 760`), and below that width the page switches to one of two declared behaviours:
      **(a) `figure.plate-scroll`** — the SVG keeps its min-width inside a horizontally scrollable plate with a
      visible edge fade + "pārvelciet ▶" label + keyboard scroll (the plate itself is focusable, `tabindex="0"`,
      `role="group"`, `aria-label`); or **(b) `figure.compact`** — a second, purpose-drawn variant with fewer labels
      and a taller canvas. Each figure chooses (a) or (b) explicitly in `figures.py`, and the choice is recorded.
- [ ] No SVG label renders below **11 px effective** at 390 px in any figure. Measured by T11's harness at three
      widths; the table of smallest label per figure per width is attached.
- [ ] At 390 px, zero sideways-scrolling *page rows* remain; only declared `plate-scroll` figures scroll, and they
      say so. `inspect.mjs` `side-scroll` drops to 0.
- [ ] 200 % browser zoom at 390 px (effective 195 px) still does not clip text; the plate scrolls instead.
- [ ] Print: one scale rule for figures — `svg { max-width: 100%; break-inside: avoid }` plus a print-specific
      minimum font rule; no figure splits across pages; the caption stays with the drawing.
- [ ] The fig-study control from T08 sits **below** the drawing on a phone, above it on desktop, and its summary is
      never the only way to see the labels.

### Task substeps
1. **Measure**, per figure: smallest label, its unit size, the width at which it hits 11 px, and whether the figure
   can lose labels.
2. **Choose the behaviour** per figure (scroll plate vs compact variant) and implement it once as a component.
3. **Verify** at 390/768/1440, at 200 % zoom, in print, and with JS off.

### Subtask 12.1 — Per-figure legibility measurement
- **12.1.a** Extend T11's harness to compute, for each figure, `min_effective_px(width) = min(font_units) *
      width / viewBox_width`, and print a table for widths 356/700/1100/1440.
- **12.1.b** For each figure, decide the minimum width at which it is legible (target 11 px), e.g. a figure whose
      smallest label is 13 units on a 760 canvas needs `≥ 643 px`.
- **12.1.c** Record the decision per figure in `build/figures.py` as `MIN_PX = …` next to the drawing function, so
      the number lives with the artwork.

### Subtask 12.2 — The two behaviours
- **12.2.a** Implement `figure.plate-scroll` once: a wrapper with `overflow-x: auto`, `overscroll-behavior-x:
      contain`, a sticky edge shadow-free fade implemented as a 1 px tone step (not a gradient — gradients are
      banned), a `::after` label "pārvelciet", and `tabindex="0"` + arrow-key scrolling.
- **12.2.b** Implement `figure.compact` as a documented alternative: a separate function in `figures.py` with the
      same `<title>`/`<desc>`, fewer labels, and a taller aspect ratio; the page swaps via CSS only
      (two SVGs, one shown per breakpoint), never via JS.
- **12.2.c** Apply the choice to all 16 figures; the three most label-dense (`fig-periodic`, `fig-dialysis`,
      `fig-molemap`) are candidates for compact variants, the axis-type figures (`fig-solubility`,
      `fig-continuum`, `fig-dispersion`) for scroll plates.

### Subtask 12.3 — Tables and print
- **12.3.a** Fix the 3 side-scrolling rows: matrix tables get a declared `plate-scroll` treatment with a sticky
      first column (already present) and a visible affordance; anything else wraps. Verify each of the 3 by id.
- **12.3.b** Add the print rules: figure cannot break inside, caption `break-before: avoid`, `svg { max-width:
      100% }`, and a print-only scale so the smallest label is ≥ 7.5 pt.
- **12.3.c** Print to PDF in Chrome, open the pages with figures, and check three specific things: no clipped axis
      label, no caption orphaned on the next page, no figure smaller than half a page.

### Gate

```bash
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
# side-scroll: 0 at 390
```
