## T13 — New figures I: the atom, the table and the bond

**Theme:** more SVGs · explanation · comprehension
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 5 · **Owner skill:** `svg-spatial-occlusion` (interaction),
`synoptic-matrix-architect` (the lattice comparison), `impeccable` (copy inside the figures) ·
**Depends on:** T10, T11, T12 (the standard, the audit, the legibility behaviour)

### Evidence
- ch02 (atoms, periodic table, REN) has 3 figures; ch03 (bonds) has 2. Both are Tier 1 (*Eksāmena kodols*).
- The existing `filling()` draws eight orbital rows; it does not show *orbital shape*, the distinction between
  s/p/d, or why 4s fills before 3d beyond a one-line caption.
- `continuum()` shows ΔREN as a number line, which is good, but there is no figure showing the *consequence*:
  ionic lattice vs shared pair vs electron sea.
- Four crystal-lattice types (ionic, atomic/covalent, molecular, metallic) are taught in words only (E15).
- `AGENTS.md` §3.2 gap 6 (bond polarity vs molecular polarity) is taught in prose with no drawing; CO₂ vs H₂O is
  the canonical trap (M10) and it deserves a picture.
- The periodic table figure shows 26 elements in a 4-period window with a d-block band; it is honest but it cannot
  carry the trend reasoning the chapter asks for.

### Intent
Give the two most foundational chapters a visual argument: the atom has structure, the table has gradients, a bond
is a continuum with consequences, and polarity is a property of the *shape*, not only the bond. Six new figures,
each doing one job, each readable at 390 px.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Six new figures exist, each in `build/figures.py` as its own function, each passing T11's audit and T12's
      legibility rule, each with `title`/`desc`/`figcaption`/source-or-`papildinājums` tag.
- [ ] Each is placed exactly once (the `{{FIG:id}}` mechanism already fails on unknown/duplicate/never-placed ids).
- [ ] Each figure's numbers come from `figdata.py` and are asserted by `check_numbers.py`.
- [ ] Each new figure adds **at least one retrieval prompt** in the chapter ("Pēc attēla: kāpēc CO₂ ir nepolāra
      molekula ar polārām saitēm?") — the deload gate counts recall coverage, currently 29 concepts / 122
      opportunities.
- [ ] Chapter figure counts after: ch02 = 3 + 3, ch03 = 2 + 3; `deload_report.py` reflects it.
- [ ] Total page size stays within the re-derived budget (T06 decides the font cost first); if the six figures
      push past it, minify the CSS before dropping a figure.

### The six figures (specification)

| # | Id | Chapter | Teaches | Data it must carry | Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 13.1 | `fig-orbitals` | ch02 | s, p and d orbital shapes and the 2n² capacity | 1s, 2s, 2p (3 boxes), 3d (5 boxes); the 2/6/10 capacities; the 2n² maxima 2, 8, 18, 32 | occlusion: mask the subshell names, review |
| 13.2 | `fig-trends` | ch02 | REN, radius and ionisation energy across a period and down a group | REN values (Pauling) for the 26 drawn elements; radius direction arrows; IE direction arrows | none (static, must print) |
| 13.3 | `fig-bond-types` | ch03 | three bonding outcomes from the same ΔREN axis: electron transfer, shared pair, electron sea | ΔREN marks 0,35 / 1,7 / 2,0; the three models: Na⁺Cl⁻, H–H, Na-metal | none |
| 13.4 | `fig-lattice-types` | ch03 | four crystal lattices as a 4-row comparison | ionic (NaCl), atomic-covalent (diamond), molecular (I₂/CO₂ solid), metallic (Cu); melting-point order; conduction yes/no | synoptic matrix, 4 attributes |
| 13.5 | `fig-polarity` | ch03 | bond polarity vs molecular polarity: CO₂ nonpolar, H₂O polar, CH₄ nonpolar | bond dipoles as arrows; net dipole = 0 / ≠ 0; bond angle 180° / 104,5° / 109,5° | occlusion: hide the net-dipole arrow, ask |
| 13.6 | `fig-hbond` | ch03 | hydrogen bond: what it is, what it is not (not inside a molecule, not any H) | O–H···O geometry, δ+ and δ−, ~5–40 kJ/mol vs O–H 463 kJ/mol; ice vs liquid | step scrubber, 3 phases |

### Task substeps
1. **Specify and draw** each figure to the standard, at the data level first (a table of constants), then the
   geometry.
2. **Place and wire** each into its chapter with the right placement, caption, source tag and retrieval prompt.
3. **Audit and read**: T11 clean, T12 legible at 390, contact sheet read as a set, and one figure rejected or
   simplified after looking at it.

### Subtask 13.1 — Orbital shapes (`fig-orbitals`)
- **13.1.a** Draw s as a circle, p as three orthogonal lobes with a nodal plane, d as five lobes; put the quantum
      labels (`n`, `l`, `mₗ`) in a reserved left band, capacity in a right band, and never inside a lobe.
- **13.1.b** Add the 2n² maxima as a small table inside the figure *as data*, not as prose: 2, 8, 18, 32, with the
      note that level 3 does not fill before 4s (E16, M30).
- **13.1.c** Occlusion mode: mask the `1s/2s/2p/3d` names and the capacities separately; the review mode asks the
      reader to point at the subshell that fills after 3p.

### Subtask 13.2 — Trends (`fig-trends`)
- **13.2.a** Reuse `periodic()`'s cell geometry but only for the main-group window; add a separate right-hand panel
      with the three trend arrows and their *reasons* in three short lines (Z↑ pulls electrons in; shells↑ push
      out; shielding).
- **13.2.b** Assert every REN value against `figdata.REN` (the same table `check_numbers.py` already verifies) and
      mark the noble gases as "–" (no Pauling value), not as 0.
- **13.2.c** Print test: 26 cells at 40 mm cell width must keep the REN readable at 7.5 pt; if not, drop the REN
      number from the cell and keep it only in the chapter table, and say so in the caption.

### Subtask 13.3 — Bond types and lattices (`fig-bond-types`, `fig-lattice-types`)
- **13.3.a** `fig-bond-types`: one horizontal ΔREN axis shared by three small panels; each panel shows the model,
      the electron bookkeeping (arrow or shared pair or sea), and the property that follows (conducts? melts?).
- **13.3.b** `fig-lattice-types`: a real `<table class="mx">` with rows ionic / atomic-covalent / molecular /
      metallic and columns example / particle / attraction / melting point / conduction / solubility — plus a small
      drawn cell for each row so the matrix has a picture (the matrix skill's own requirement: a legend next to
      its diagram).
- **13.3.c** Both figures must carry the E15 terminology decision (*atomu (kovalentais) kristālrežģis*) in their
      caption, not in a footnote, because that is the term the exam will ask for.

### Subtask 13.3b — second half: polarity and the hydrogen bond (`fig-polarity`, `fig-hbond`)
- **13.4.a** `fig-polarity`: three molecules side by side at the same scale, bond dipoles as small arrows, the net
      dipole drawn as one larger arrow or a struck-through zero; label "polāras saites, nepolāra molekula" for CO₂
      — the sentence the reader must be able to say.
- **13.4.b** `fig-hbond`: a three-phase scrubber (atoms → δ+ δ− interaction → network in ice) with a kJ/mol
      comparison bar (5–40 vs 463) drawn to scale, and an explicit "nav" mark on CH₄.
- **13.4.c** Wire the scrubber using the existing `SCRUBS` data model (complete snapshots, no interpolation, static
      transcript for no-JS/print) so `check_components.py` covers it for free.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/build_master.py && python3 build/check_components.py
python3 build/check_svg.py --widths 356,700,1100,1440
python3 build/check_numbers.py
python3 build/deload_report.py | grep -E 'ch02|ch03'
```

### Guardrails
- Do not copy a textbook figure. Every drawing is original; cite the *idea* in the caption, never a picture
  (`AGENTS.md` §5).
- Do not put text over a lobe, a cell or a bond. Labels go in bands with leaders.
- Do not introduce a fourth semantic colour for figures. The figure tokens are tones of the same three roles.

## T14 — New figures II: mixtures, solutions and reaction energetics

**Theme:** more SVGs · explanation · addon
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 5 · **Owner skill:** `state-scrubber-lab` (dissolution and energy
profiles), `synoptic-matrix-architect` (solubility grid), `svg-spatial-occlusion` (osmosis) ·
**Depends on:** T10, T11, T12

### Evidence
- ch04 (mixtures, dispersed systems) has 2 figures and a 2-factor classification; ch05 (solution, solubility) has
  2; ch06 (concentration) has 1; ch11 (reactions) has 1; ch14 (organism) has 0.
- The solubility table is "a picture in D p.6" and `AGENTS.md` §3.2 gap 3 explicitly says the master must teach
  how to read it. The chapter has a table and a curve figure, but no figure that makes the *table itself* legible.
- Heat effects (exo/endothermic) are Tier 3 and are taught in words and numbers (E46) with no energy profile.
- Isotonic/hypertonic solutions appear in ch14 with no diagram; `0,9 % NaCl ≈ 308 mOsm/L` and `5 % glucose =
  278 mmol/L` are verified numbers in `SOURCE_LEDGER.md` §3 and deserve to be drawn.
- Colloids are taught with a size axis but not with the optical property (Tyndall) that identifies them.

### Intent
Make the physical picture visible: what dissolving costs and pays, what a solubility table encodes, why a
colloid looks the way it does, why a reaction warms or cools, and why 0,9 % is the number it is. Five figures
plus one interactive table.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Six new figures/one interactive table exist, each passing T11 and T12 and carrying its source tag.
- [ ] The solubility grid is a real `<table>` (not an SVG picture) with the four symbol classes, an explanation of
      each symbol, and a "choose two ions" mode that shows whether a precipitate forms — offline, no network.
- [ ] ch04 = 2 + 2, ch05 = 2 + 1 (+ the grid), ch06 = 1 + 1, ch11 = 1 + 1, ch14 = 0 + 1.
- [ ] Every number in the new figures is asserted: 308 mOsm/L, 278 mmol/L, 0,9 %, 5 %, 22,4 L/mol, the four
      solubility classes, the Tyndall wavelengths (no invented values).
- [ ] Each new figure is accompanied by a "ko ievērot" caption and one retrieval prompt.

### The six specifications

| # | Id | Chapter | Teaches | Data | Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14.1 | `fig-dissolve` | ch05 | dissolving as three energy steps: break lattice (+), break water H-bonds (+), hydrate (−) | qualitative signs only; the net sign decides warming/cooling; NH₄NO₃ vs NaOH as the two outcomes | scrubber, 3 phases |
| 14.2 | `fig-solgrid` | ch05 | how to read the solubility table | the four classes (šķīst / maz šķīst / praktiski nešķīst / –) with the exact g/100 g edges from E18 | interactive: pick cation + anion → verdict + net ionic equation |
| 14.3 | `fig-colloid` | ch04 | Tyndall scattering and Brownian motion: why a colloid looks clear but scatters | particle size 1–100 nm vs wavelength 400–700 nm; no invented "typical" values | toggle: true solution / colloid / suspension beam |
| 14.4 | `fig-osmosis` | ch14 | osmosis, isotonic / hypotonic / hypertonic, and the two clinical numbers | 0,9 % NaCl ≈ 308 mOsm/L; 5 % glucose = 278 mmol/L; cell volume arrows | scrubber, 3 states |
| 14.5 | `fig-energy` | ch11 | exothermic vs endothermic profiles; activation energy; catalyst | ΔH signs; the E46 numbers (CO₂ 393,5; propane 2043/2220; ethanol 1235/1367) | toggle: with/without catalyst |
| 14.6 | `fig-dilution` | ch06 | dilution: moles constant, volume grows, concentration falls | c₁V₁ = c₂V₂ with the B #14/#15 numbers 6,88 → 1,00 mol/L | scrubber, 4 states |

### Task substeps
1. **Data first.** Put every constant in `figdata.py` with its source tag; assert before drawing.
2. **Draw to the standard** and wire the interactions with the existing components (`SCRUB:id`, `MX:id`).
3. **Read and prune**: contact sheet, 390 px check, and remove any figure that repeats its chapter's table.

### Subtask 14.1 — Dissolution and dilution
- **14.1.a** `fig-dissolve`: three stacked plates (lattice → separated ions → hydrated ions) with energy arrows
      whose *direction* is the message; label the net line "ja šķīšana atņem enerģiju → šķīdums kļūst auksts".
- **14.1.b** `fig-dilution`: particles drawn as counts (e.g. 8 particles in 1 unit volume → 4 in 2 units), not as
      a colour change; add the arithmetic strip `c₁V₁ = c₂V₂` with the real numbers from `figdata`.
- **14.1.c** Both are scrubbers with complete snapshots; verify the static transcript in no-JS and print matches
      the last phase, and that `check_components.py` passes.

### Subtask 14.2 — The solubility grid (`fig-solgrid`)
- **14.2.a** Model the grid as data: rows = cations (Na⁺, K⁺, NH₄⁺, Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, Ba²⁺, Al³⁺, Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺, Cu²⁺, Zn²⁺,
      Ag⁺, Pb²⁺), columns = anions (NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, CO₃²⁻, PO₄³⁻, OH⁻, S²⁻); each cell one of four classes.
      Every cell cites D p.6 or is marked *papildinājums* with a reference.
- **14.2.b** Build the interactive mode as a `<form>`: two `<select>`s + a button → a verdict line, the formula,
      and the net ionic equation when a precipitate forms. All data inline; no network; JS off = the plain table.
- **14.2.c** Teach the symbol grammar explicitly in the caption and in a legend row: what "maz šķīst" means
      numerically (E18's corrected edges), how temperature qualifiers are shown, and why "–" (no data) is not
      "insoluble".

### Subtask 14.3 — Colloid, osmosis, energy
- **14.3.a** `fig-colloid`: one beam figure with three panels (solution / colloid / suspension), the scattering
      drawn as rays, and a size-vs-wavelength scale beneath — the only honest way to explain why 1–100 nm matters.
- **14.3.b** `fig-osmosis`: three cells in three solutions, water-movement arrows, and the two clinical numbers as
      a small comparison table inside the figure; mark 5 % glucose as *isotonic before metabolism* (M31), because
      that nuance is exactly what a medical student is asked about.
- **14.3.c** `fig-energy`: two profiles drawn on the same axes with the same ΔH scale, a catalyst curve as a dashed
      variant, and the E46 numbers as labels; state the water state (g/l) next to each ΔH, because that is the
      error E46 documents.

## T15 — New figures III: acid–base, hydrolysis, redox and the body

**Theme:** more SVGs · explanation · the four hardest chapters
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 5 · **Owner skill:** `state-scrubber-lab` (half-reaction ladder),
`synoptic-matrix-architect` (hydrolysis matrix), `svg-spatial-occlusion` (pH scale) · **Depends on:** T10–T12

### Evidence
- ch07 (electrolytes), ch09 (hydrolysis), ch10 (compound classes) and ch12 (redox) have **0 figures each**, and
  they are the four chapters where the reasoning is most abstract.
- ch07 also has 10 blocks before its first `h3` — a wall of prose with no visual anchor (`deload_report.py`
  `pre-h3=10`).
- The half-reaction method (KMnO₄ + H₂O₂, A p.14) is taught as a scrubber in text; the electron bookkeeping is the
  one thing a diagram does better than prose.
- Standard potentials exist as a table in the sources (E s.48, with E47's errors) and in prose, but not as a
  visual ordering that lets a student *predict* a reaction.
- The pH figure exists (15 swatches) but there is no logarithmic scale figure, which is where students actually
  fail (M19: ten-fold dilution taking pH past 7).

### Intent
Put a picture behind every one of the four abstract chapters. Where the chapter's content is a *classification*,
use a matrix; where it is a *process*, use a scrubber; where it is a *scale*, use the logarithmic axis. Five
figures.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Five new figures, each passing T11/T12, each with its source/`papildinājums` tag, each earning a retrieval
      prompt.
- [ ] ch07 = 0 + 1 (+ the existing `{{VS:…}}` component retained), ch09 = 0 + 1, ch10 = 0 + 2, ch12 = 0 + 3
      (one of which is the potentials ordering).
- [ ] The half-reaction staircase is checked arithmetic: every electron count, every charge balance, asserted in
      `check_numbers.py` (KMnO₄ + H₂O₂ in acid: 2 MnO₄⁻ + 5 H₂O₂ + 6 H⁺ → 2 Mn²⁺ + 5 O₂ + 8 H₂O).
- [ ] The hydrolysis matrix is a real `<table class="mx">` with per-cell reveal and a difference highlight, not a
      picture of a table.
- [ ] The pH figures (existing `fig-ph` and the new log scale) agree: 15 swatches, numbers beneath, neutral at
      7,00 @ 25 °C and ≈ 6,8 @ 37 °C stated in the caption.
- [ ] ch07's 10-block prose wall is split by at least three `h3` headings as part of this task (the figure needs
      somewhere to sit, and the reader needs signposts).

### The five specifications

| # | Id | Chapter | Teaches | Data | Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15.1 | `fig-ioncount` | ch07 | why one formula unit gives 2/3/4/5 ions; strong vs weak dissociation | NaCl 2, Na₂SO₄ 3, Na₃PO₄ 4, AlCl₃ 4, Al₂(SO₄)₃ 5 (B #8); α schemes E25 both | occlusion: hide the ion counts |
| 15.2 | `fig-hydrolysis` | ch09 | four salt types × what hydrolyses × pH direction | the four rows of ch09's table; Al₂S₃ complete hydrolysis; NH₄CH₃COO ≈ 7 by coincidence | matrix with per-cell reveal |
| 15.3 | `fig-halfrxn` | ch12 | balancing a redox reaction as a four-step staircase | KMnO₄ + H₂O₂: oxidation numbers, half-reactions, electron count 10, final coefficients | scrubber, 4 phases |
| 15.4 | `fig-potentials` | ch12 | reading standard reduction potentials and predicting direction | the potentials of E s.48, with E47's three corrections applied and marked | sortable ordering, no JS dependency |
| 15.5 | `fig-phlog` | ch08 | pH as a logarithmic scale; dilution and the neutral point | 10⁻¹ … 10⁻¹⁴, neutral 7,00 @ 25 °C / 6,8 @ 37 °C; ten-fold dilution = 1 pH unit | scrubber: add water, watch pH |

### Task substeps
1. **Choose the right component per chapter** — a matrix for ch09/ch07, a scrubber for ch12, a scale for ch08 —
   and write the reason in the task note (why not the other component).
2. **Draw and wire**, with all arithmetic asserted.

- **15.1.a** `fig-ioncount`: five formula units drawn at a constant scale, ions separated by charge, count printed

- **15.2.a** `fig-halfrxn`: four phases — assign oxidation states, split into half-reactions, balance electrons

**Theme:** understandableness · copy · pedagogy
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 6 · **Owner skill:** `cognitive-deload-auditor` (six-point gate),
`impeccable` (`clarify` reference for copy) · **Depends on:** T01 (terms fixed), T03 (one text metric),
T13–T15 (figures exist to point at)

### Evidence
- The chapters are dense but unevenly scaffolded. ch07 opens with a 5-row table, then `{{VS:…}}`, then a
  correction pair, then the `lead` paragraph, then "Kāpēc", then a details — **10 blocks before the first `h3`**
  (`pre-h3=10`). ch09 has 5.
- The `lead` paragraph in ch09 appears *after* the table it introduces, and in ch07 also after the table — the
  "what you will be able to do" sentence arrives after the reader has already met the hardest artefact.
- The existing pedagogy has four good patterns (`why1` one-liner, `details.why` "why not X", `details.deep`,
  `prompt-peer` self-explanation) but they are not applied consistently: 41 `.deep` for 17 chapters; a single
  `callout prompt-peer` in the whole page.
- The six-point deload report scores every chapter identically, which means it is not discriminating — partly the
  metric bug in F22/T03, partly because it does not measure the *order* of explanation.
- Numeric density: 1,216 substantive paragraphs, 2,709 sentences, average 9.8 words per sentence — the sentences
  are already short; the problem is not length but **sequencing and signposting**.

### Intent
Every Tier 1 concept should be reachable in three moves: recognise it, explain it, use it. That is a *reasoning
ladder*, and the page currently has rungs in different orders in different chapters. Standardise the ladder, make
the "why not" the default rather than an occasional treat, and make the first screen of each chapter tell the
reader what they will be able to do *before* they meet the artefact.

### Definition of done
- [ ] A chapter template, written into `build/CHAPTER_TEMPLATE.md`, with a fixed order for the first five blocks:
      (1) **Ko jāprot** (verbs, tier word), (2) **lead** — one sentence of what and one of why it matters,
      (3) **the simplest artefact** (a definition or a 2-line example, never a matrix), (4) **Piemērs** with
      numbers, (5) **Attēls** or **Biežākās kļūdas**, in that order. Every chapter conforms or states in the
      changelog why it deviates.
- [ ] Each Tier 1 concept has three rungs, labelled in plain words (no decorative labels): *atpazīt* (a recognisable
      signal), *izskaidrot* (a why-sentence), *lietot* (a worked use). A table of 27 Tier 1 concepts × 3 rungs is
      the checklist; missing rungs are listed, not hidden.
- [ ] Every chapter has at least one `details.why` phrased as **"Kāpēc nevis X?"** where X is the specific wrong
      belief from the mistake seeds — currently the strongest pattern on the page and the least used.
- [ ] Every chapter has at least one `prompt-peer` self-explanation prompt (currently 1 in 17 chapters).
- [ ] Every `Skaidrojums` section defines each new term at first use *in the sentence that needs it*, and the build
      asserts it (27 Tier-1 + ionic equations already pass `check_definitions.py`; extend to Tier 2–3 at ≥ 60 %).
- [ ] Zero figure captions used as prose. Captions are one sentence of "ko ievērot"; explanation moves into the
      body (this also fixes the false-positive paragraph counts).
- [ ] The six-point deload gate reports *differently* per chapter after the change, and the recall-coverage ratio
      is printed: distinct concepts with a retrieval prompt / inventory size (target 1.00 Tier 1, ≥ 0.60 Tier 2–3).

### Task substeps
1. **Diagnose per chapter** with a fixed rubric (rungs present, first-open order, why-not count, self-explanation
   count, term-at-first-use, caption/prose split) and write the scores into `build/reasoning-audit.md`.
2. **Rewrite in place**, chapter by chapter, never in one pass: each chapter is a separate commit so a regression
   can be bisected.
3. **Measure again** with the same rubric and show the before/after table.

### Subtask 16.1 — The rubric and the ladder
- **16.1.a** Write `build/reasoning_audit.py` that computes, per chapter: index of the first `h3`; whether `lead`
      precedes the first table/figure; count of `details.why`, `details.deep`, `.why1`, `.prompt-peer`; count of
      Tier-1 concepts with a retrieval prompt; count of undefined first uses (reuse `definitions.py`).
- **16.1.b** Build the 27-concept ladder table by hand into `build/ladder.md` (concept · recognise · explain ·
      use · where each rung lives today · what is missing). This is a judgement document; it must be reviewed, not
      generated.
- **16.1.c** Freeze the audit output as the baseline in `build/reasoning-baseline.json`, so later changes are
      measured against it.

### Subtask 16.2 — Chapter surgery (highest-value first)
- **16.2.a** ch07: move the `lead` above the table, split the 10-block wall into "Kas vada strāvu" / "Elektrolīts
      vai nav" / "Cik stipri (α)" with the new `fig-ioncount` in the middle, and convert the Cu/CaO/Cl₂ traps into
      three `Kāpēc nevis X?` details instead of one table (the table stays as the summary).
- **16.2.b** ch12 and ch13: convert each "bookkeeping" step into a numbered procedure with a check line after it
      ("Pārbaude: lādiņu summa abās pusēs vienāda?"), because these are the chapters where a student can produce a
      plausible wrong number with no way to notice.
- **16.2.c** ch01, ch14: add one medical anchor each *inside the first three blocks*, not in a context section at
      the end, so the "why should a medic care" question is answered before the reader decides the page is
      irrelevant.

### Subtask 16.3 — Copy pass
- **16.3.a** Remove every "In this section…"-style opener in Latvian ("Šajā nodaļā aplūkosim…"), which the tells
      registry bans in its English form and which the page uses in several places; replace with the outcome in
      verbs.
- **16.3.b** Convert the 27 over-length paragraphs (the honest number after T03's fix) into a list or a 2-paragraph
      split; never by deleting content.
- **16.3.c** Add the "kas mainījās kopš avota" one-liner to each chapter opening where a ledger correction touches
      its core claim, so the reader knows the page is not a transcript before they invest 20 minutes.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/reasoning_audit.py --json | tee /tmp/reasoning.json
python3 build/check_text.py --max-sentences 4 --max-words 65
python3 build/deload_report.py
# recall coverage printed: tier1 >= 1.00, tier2-3 >= 0.60
```

### Guardrails
- Do not rewrite a chapter that already scores well just to make the numbers uniform. The rubric is a floor.
- Do not convert prose into bullet lists everywhere: the cognitive-deload gate wants ≤ 4-sentence paragraphs and
  visual signalling, not fragment-speak.
- Do not change a sourced sentence's meaning while shortening it. Every rewrite keeps its `[source]` tag and, if
  the claim changed, gets a new tag.

## T17 — The problem-solving system: limiting reagent, yield, error injection

**Theme:** understandableness · functionality · addon
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 6 · **Owner skill:** `state-scrubber-lab` (decision tree),
`cognitive-deload-auditor` · **Depends on:** T16 (procedure language), T15 (`fig-halfrxn` reuses the same check
discipline)

### Evidence
- ch13 is the strongest chapter (2 figures, 191 numeric assertions) but the *method* is still prose: the three-stage
  route is a figure, the limiting-reagent case is solved once (B #13), and there is no yield problem at all.
- `AGENTS.md` §3.2 gap 2 says limiting reagent is a named procedure the lectures never name. The page names it but
  does not give a decision procedure with a stopping rule.
- 43 self-test items and 12 error-hunt statements exist, but there is no "find the error in this worked solution"
  practice with the *page's own* numbers — the highest-value retrieval format for calculation chapters.
- Every intermediate already carries `data-exact`/`data-expr`, so the build can generate both a correct and a
  deliberately wrong variant of any solution line without hand-authoring them.

### Intent
Turn calculation from "reproduce the example" into "run a procedure with checkpoints". Add the two things the
course is missing (limiting reagent as a procedure, yield as a concept), and use the number machine the build
already has to generate error-injection drills that cannot drift from the correct answers.

### Definition of done
- [ ] A named procedure, **"Ierobežojošais reaģents: 5 soļi"**, presented as a numbered list with a stopping rule
      ("ja b/a ir mazākais, B ir ierobežojošais"), a worked B #13, and a counter-example that compares grams and
      fails (M04). One figure (a decision tree or a ratio strip) and one table.
- [ ] A **yield** section: theoretical vs actual, `% = actual / theoretical × 100`, marked *papildinājums* (not in
      the lectures), with one worked example whose numbers `check_numbers.py` asserts and one "why is yield never
      100 %" paragraph that names no invented industrial figure.
- [ ] **Error injection**: at least 8 statements of the form "Šajā risinājumā ir viena kļūda — atrodiet to", each
      generated from a correct `dl.calc` block by a transform in `build/quiz.py` (`swap coefficient`, `drop a unit
      conversion`, `use the solute mass instead of the solution mass`, `compare grams`, `forget the dilution
      factor`), with the wrongness asserted by `check_numbers.py`.
- [ ] A **checkpoint checklist** printed after every worked problem: units, significant figures, mass balance,
      charge balance, limiting reagent, plausibility. The list is one block, linked, not repeated per problem.
- [ ] All numbers in the new material are script-generated; hand-typed intermediates are forbidden (the existing
      `data-expr` mechanism enforces it).

### Task substeps
1. **Write the procedure** and its figure; test it against B #12, #13 and one new case.
2. **Add yield** with a verified example and a "why not 100 %" paragraph.
3. **Generate the error drills** from existing solutions and wire them into ch16, not ch15 (practice ≠ test).

### Subtask 17.1 — Limiting reagent
- **17.1.a** Write the five steps as a `dl` or `ol` with the stopping rule in bold: 1 balance; 2 convert all
      reagents to n; 3 divide each n by its coefficient; 4 the smallest quotient is limiting; 5 compute the product
      from the limiting reagent only.
- **17.1.b** Add the ratio-strip figure: for each reagent, a bar scaled to `n/coefficient`, the shortest bar marked
      "ierobežojošais". Use the B #13 numbers (0,1604 / 0,0918 with coefficients 2 and 1) so the reader can check
      the drawing against the solved problem.
- **17.1.c** Add the counter-example: "9 g KOH un 9 g H₂SO₄ — grami vienādi, moli nav" with the two quotients
      shown; assert `0,0802` and `0,0918` in `check_numbers.py`.

### Subtask 17.2 — Yield
- **17.2.a** Define theoretical yield from the limiting reagent, then actual, then `%`; state explicitly that
      ``papildinājums`` — the lectures do not define yield, and the exam may not use it.
- **17.2.b** Work one example end-to-end on the B #10 Ca(OH)₂ + HCl reaction, with `check_numbers.py` asserting
      every line; choose round numbers so the arithmetic does not obscure the concept.
- **17.2.c** Add the "why not 100 %" paragraph naming only mechanisms (incomplete reaction, side reactions,
      losses in transfer, impure reagent) with no invented percentages.

### Subtask 17.3 — Error injection
- **17.3.a** Implement `mutate(block)` in `build/quiz.py`: parse a `dl.calc` block, apply one named transform,
      recompute with the *wrong* expression so the displayed wrong answer is internally consistent, and emit the
      statement + the error id + the fix.
- **17.3.b** Author the 8 transforms and their explanations; each explanation must say *why the wrong move feels
      right* (that is the mistake-seed pattern, M01–M32).
- **17.3.c** Place them in ch16 as a `<details>` set with the answer behind a reveal, and assert in
      `check_numbers.py` that each mutated line is indeed inconsistent with the given inputs.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_numbers.py          # includes yield + mutated lines
python3 build/check_quiz.py             # if absent: build it — 8 drills, 0 answer leaks
python3 build/check_components.py
```

### Guardrails
- Yield is *papildinājums*. It must never appear as if the course taught it, and it must not push the Tier 1 core
  down.
- Do not let an error drill show the correct answer in the same `details` summary.
- Do not introduce normality, molality or any unit the sources do not use (`SOURCE_LEDGER.md` §2 bans them).

## T18 — Re-audit of sources, numbers and the 32 `[jāpārbauda]` items

**Theme:** correctness · trust
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 6 · **Owner skill:** none (research + `ledger.py`), reviewed by a
human · **Depends on:** T01 (terms stable), T15 (potentials figure shows E47 flags)

### Evidence
- 32 `[jāpārbauda]` markers remain in the page; `ledger.py:verified` holds the subset that has a named reference.
- 61 E ids exist; every one is required to appear either inline or in the appendix (`c_corrections` asserts the
  count and the links).
- The figure data now becomes load-bearing (T10.3): solubility points, ΔREN values, REN table, pH colours and — once
  T15 lands — standard potentials. A single wrong constant in `figdata.py` would propagate to a figure, a caption
  and a quiz answer at once.
- E47 lists three potentials that are wrong in the source (`Br₂/2Br⁻ +0,96` should be ≈ +1,07; `O₂/H₂O +1,21865`
  should be +1,229; `PbO₂/Pb²⁺ +1,80` should be +1,455). These are currently flagged, not corrected.
- E01 fixes N_A to 6,022·10²³ across three sources; E59 fixes four arithmetic/typo errors in D p.19–20.

### Intent
Convert every "probably right" into either "checked against X" or "still unverified, and here is why". The value of
this page is that it can be trusted more than the PDFs it replaces; a single unflagged wrong constant destroys that
in one reading.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Every `[jāpārbauda]` item is resolved into exactly one of: **verified** (with the named reference written into
      `ledger.py:verified` and the page showing `pārbaudīts: <reference>`), **kept unverified** (with a one-line
      reason and an explicit reader warning), or **withdrawn** (the claim is removed and the withdrawal is logged).
- [ ] The count of `[jāpārbauda]` is reported in the final report with one line per item — this is already required
      by `MASTER_PROMPT.md` §10.5 and must actually happen.
- [ ] `figdata.py` is asserted against `SOURCE_LEDGER.md` §3 for every constant, and a "figure data" row appears in
      `check-report.json`.
- [ ] The potentials figure does not silently "fix" E47; it shows the source value, the flagged value, and the
      corrected value only when a reference is named.
- [ ] Clinical constants (blood pH 7,35–7,45; core temperature ≈ 36,1–37,5 °C; total body water ≈ 50–60 %) have a
      named reference or carry the unverified flag. No invented ranges.
- [ ] A "Labojumu statuss" table in the appendix shows, for each E id: shown inline / appendix only / verified /
      unverified, generated from `ledger.py`, not typed.

### Task substeps
1. **Extract the pending list** programmatically with the surrounding claim, the source page and the reason it is
   pending.
2. **Resolve** each with a reference (IUPAC Gold Book, CRC Handbook, a named textbook, a clinical reference). Where
   no reference is available offline, keep the flag and write the reason.
3. **Propagate**: update `ledger.py`, the figure data, the appendix status table, and the final report.

### Subtask 18.1 — The pending register
- **18.1.a** Add `--pending` to `ledger.py` that prints `{id, claim, source_page, basis, current_label}` for all 32,
      so the list is generated rather than recalled.
- **18.1.b** Group them by domain (atomic structure, bonding, solutions, acid–base, redox/potentials, medical) —
      each domain can be verified against one authority, which is faster and less error-prone than item by item.
- **18.1.c** For each group, name the authority in `ledger.py:verified[group]` and record the edition/year, because
      "checked against CRC" without an edition is not a citation.

### Subtask 18.2 — Resolution
- **18.2.a** Potentials (E47): verify the three values, then render the figure with the source value struck through,
      the corrected value, and the reference; if a value cannot be verified, the figure keeps the flag.
- **18.2.b** Bonding/ΔREN (E10, E12, E13): verify the cutoffs and the π/σ energy ratio against a named source; the
      figure already shows both cutoffs, so only the reference changes.
- **18.2.c** Medical constants (E48–E51, E54–E57): verify or flag each; the page must not silently pick a range.

### Subtask 18.3 — Propagation and status table
- **18.3.a** Make `build_master.py::block_tag` read only from `ledger.py:verified` (it already does) and add the
      appendix status table generated from the same source.
- **18.3.b** Re-assert `figdata.py` constants and add a gate step `c_figdata`.
- **18.3.c** Write the final-report pending list (one line per unresolved id) into `build/check-report.json` so the
      report step is mechanical.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/ledger.py --pending            # 32 → N resolved, M still open with reasons
python3 build/check_numbers.py
python3 build/check_claims.py                # every X-basis correction labelled
grep -c 'jāpārbauda' Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html
```

### Guardrails
- Never present an X-basis correction as the lecturer's words (`AGENTS.md` §5).
- Never delete a source statement to avoid dealing with it; show it, then correct it.
- If a reference cannot be consulted offline in this workspace, the item stays flagged. Inventing a citation is a
  worse failure than leaving the flag.

## T19 — Accessibility, breakpoints, and the print edition

**Theme:** functionality · accessibility · print
**Priority:** P1 · **Effort:** M · **Wave:** 6 · **Owner skill:** `audit` (technical), `break-ui` (stress),
`print-css-alchemist` (print) · **Depends on:** T05–T12 (surfaces, type, controls, figures)

### Evidence
- 768 px: off-centre margins 31 px left / 47 px right (F18).
- 390 px: 3 rows scroll sideways with clipped content (F19; overlaps T12).
- 22 inline reveal buttons named only "nē" / "< 1 nm" (F17).
- No skip link (F15; T07 fixes the navigation half).
- 6,228 characters of print CSS already exist and do real work (`@page`, running heads, `target-counter`,
  break rules), so the print edition is close — it needs verification, not a rewrite.
- Contrast is currently good on the page palette (ink 14.92, muted 6.69, def 8.59, link 6.20, err 7.81, fix 7.01,
  focus 6.20) but fails inside figures (white on `#c9604f` = 3.99) and on faded text (F11, F12).

### Intent
Ship the page to a reader who uses a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, 200 % zoom, and a printer — without
changing the design's character. Then make the print edition a real artefact: answers open, page numbers correct,
no clipped figure, no split table.

### Definition of done
- [ ] Skip link present and first in tab order; `main` has `id="main"` and `tabindex="-1"`.
- [ ] Every interactive element has an accessible name that states effect + object; zero names < 4 chars; zero
      unnamed inputs; every `aria-expanded`/`aria-pressed` toggles a real state change.
- [ ] Focus visible on every control at ≥ 3:1 against both adjacent colours; focus never hidden behind the sticky
      rail; no `outline: none` anywhere.
- [ ] 768 px margins equal within 1 px (fix the actual cause, do not add a compensating margin).
- [ ] 390 px: 0 page-level horizontal scroll; only declared plate-scroll regions scroll, with an affordance.
- [ ] 200 % zoom at 1440 and at 390: no clipping, no overlap, no loss of the tier line.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion`: no transitions except the 160 ms disclosure; verify by emulating the media feature.
- [ ] Screens read correctly with a screen reader (test with one, e.g. Orca or VoiceOver via Chrome): heading order
      without skips, landmarks named, 43 quiz items announce as one group each, the figure study mode announces its
      state once.
- [ ] Print: answers open (`beforeprint`), every figure whole, every table whole or split at a row boundary, page
      numbers in the contents correct, no link URLs printed for internal links, ink-safe colours, and a spot check
      of 10 printed pages by eye.
- [ ] A11y budgets in the gate: `build/check_a11y.py` (accessible names, target size, focus order, contrast on
      composited colours) with 0 violations.

### Task substeps
1. **Fix the structural a11y issues** (names, skip link, landmarks, focus) with a script that audits, not by hand.
2. **Fix the two layout bugs** (768 margins, 390 scroll) by finding the cause in the box model.
3. **Verify print** by rendering a PDF and reading pages, then lock the print rules with a screenshot diff.

### Subtask 19.1 — Accessible names and focus
- **19.1.a** Write `build/check_a11y.py` using the same CDP harness as T11: collect every focusable element's
      accessible name (via `el.accessibleName`-equivalent computation or a conservative approximation), role,
      state and bounding box; flag names < 4 chars, missing `aria-label` on icon-like controls, targets < 44 px at
      390, and any `outline: none`.
- **19.1.b** Fix the 22 short buttons by generating `aria-label="{question text}"` from the model (the same data
      used for the quiz), keeping the visible word.
- **19.1.c** Add a visible `:focus-visible` ring token (`--focus` already exists at 6.2:1) applied globally, and a
      `:focus` fallback for older engines; verify against the rail surface, the table header and the figure plate.

### Subtask 19.2 — The two layout bugs
- **19.2.a** Diagnose the 768 px asymmetry: inspect computed padding/margin of `.layout`, `main`, `.rail` and the
      scrollbar gutter. Likely cause: a grid with `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 14rem` collapsing and one
      side keeping its gap. Fix by making the rail `display: none` at that breakpoint and resetting the grid gap,
      not by adding margin.
- **19.2.b** Diagnose the 3 side-scrolling rows: identify the exact elements (matrix wrappers, `.eq`, a table with a
      long formula). Apply the T12 plate-scroll pattern or wrap; assert 0 page-level overflow at 390.
- **19.2.c** Screenshot both breakpoints before/after and compare with the inspector's numbers, not by eye.

### Subtask 19.3 — Print edition
- **19.3.a** Verify the `beforeprint`/`afterprint` handlers open and restore every `<details>` (270 of them) and
      that the restore is exact; add a test page that asserts the count.
- **19.3.b** Add `break-inside: avoid` for `figure`, `table.data tr`, `dl.calc`, `.pair`, `.mist`, `.defn`; and
      `break-after: avoid` for every `h2`/`h3` so a heading is never last on a page.
- **19.3.c** Render the PDF with Chrome headless, count pages, and screenshot 10 pages with figures/tables; check
      the three classic failures — clipped axis labels, a table header orphaned from its body, and a figure forced
      to half size.

### Gate
```bash
python3 build/check_a11y.py --widths 1440,768,390
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
# off-centre 0, side-scroll 0
google-chrome --headless --print-to-pdf=/tmp/chem1.pdf Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html
```

### Guardrails
- Do not add `aria-label` text that duplicates visible text verbatim where a `<label>`/`<summary>` would do; the
  rule is "accessible name = effect + object", not "more ARIA".
- Do not set `user-scalable=no` or a maximum-scale.
- Do not "fix" print by hiding the problem element in print.

## T20 — Study-loop addons: review queue, error log, exam simulator, progress

**Theme:** useful features · addon · pedagogy
**Priority:** P2 · **Effort:** L · **Wave:** 7 · **Owner skill:** `learn-then-test` (as a *separate* page only if
it stays separate — see guardrails), `cognitive-deload-auditor` · **Depends on:** T07 (navigation), T09 (search
index), T16 (ladder), T17 (drills)

### Evidence
- The page already stores two things in `localStorage` (4 call sites) — the "Zinu / Jāatkārto" mark and the
  two-pass preference — but there is no way to *use* those marks: no queue, no resurfacing, no export.
- 43 self-test items + 12 error-hunt statements + 62 corrections is enough material for a real review loop; the
  page currently presents them as a flat list.
- ch16 has a `sim-form` / `startSim` / `finishSim` timer (visible in the JS inventory), so an exam mode exists in
  embryo. It is not described anywhere a reader can find, and it has no scoring per tier or pass threshold.
- The course's own threshold is ≥ 55 % (`1_Temata apraksts 2020.pdf`), so an exam mode that does not model 55 %
  is missing the one number the student cares about.

### Intent
Make the page stop being a document and start being a study loop: mark → queue → revisit → score → see what is
weak. Everything local, everything optional, everything working with JS off (as a static list with checkboxes on
paper).

### Definition of done
- [ ] **Error log**: every mistake seed M01–M32 has a row a reader can mark "es to izdarīju" with an optional
      one-line note; stored under one key, versioned, exportable/importable as JSON, and rendered as a "Manas
      kļūdas" list with links to the block that teaches the fix.
- [ ] **Review queue**: a schedule over the 43 self-test items + 12 error hunts + 32 seeds, using a simple
      Leitner-style interval (1 / 3 / 7 / 21 days) — no algorithm the reader cannot predict, and a visible
      explanation of the intervals. Shows "šodien jāatkārto: N".
- [ ] **Exam simulator v2**: a timed run that (a) declares its composition by tier, (b) scores per tier, (c) applies
      the 55 % threshold explicitly, (d) shows the item-level result with the explanation and the mistake seed, and
      (e) never reuses a question a reader has already answered *in the last 24 h* (so practice ≠ test).
- [ ] **Progress dashboard**: one small table — chapters read (by scroll position, only if the reader opts in),
      items answered, accuracy per tier, top three error seeds. No charts, no streak gamification.
- [ ] **Export / import / reset**: one JSON blob, a copy button, a paste field, a reset with confirmation. Never a
      `fetch`.
- [ ] All of it is optional: with `localStorage` unavailable or JS off, the page behaves exactly as today, and the
      features are *absent* rather than broken.
- [ ] The data model is documented in `build/README.md` with a schema and a version number; a corrupt or older blob
      is discarded silently (with a visible note), never crashes the page.
- [ ] Prints as a **flashcard sheet**: 43 prompts with the answers on the back, 4 per A4 page with cut guides —
      which is the no-JS version of the review queue.

### Task substeps
1. **Store.** One namespaced, versioned key with a migration function and a try/catch around every access.
2. **Loop.** Queue + simulator + dashboard, all reading the same records.
3. **Escape hatch.** Export/import/print/reset, and a JS-off audit proving nothing is required.

### Subtask 20.1 — Data layer
- **20.1.a** Define `{v:2, marks:{qid:"know"|"again"}, seeds:{M01:{hit:3,note:"…"}}, attempts:[{qid,ts,correct,tier}],
      read:{ch:{at}}, prefs:{twopass,rail}}`; write a `load()/save()` pair with schema check and a migration from the
      current two keys so no existing mark is lost.
- **20.1.b** Wrap every access in `try{}catch{}` and degrade to an in-memory object; the page must never throw
      because storage is blocked (private mode, file:// in some browsers).
- **20.1.c** Add `build/check_storage.js` (node) that imports the pure functions (extract them into a small module
      inlined at build time) and tests: migration, corrupt blob, quota error, export→import round trip.

### Subtask 20.2 — Review loop
- **20.2.a** Build the queue from marks + attempts with the fixed intervals; render "Šodien jāatkārto (N)" at the
      top of ch16 with a start button that walks the queue one item at a time with keyboard `1`/`2`/`3`.
- **20.2.b** Build the error log as a table of 32 seeds with a mark control, a note field and a link to the
      teaching block; sort by "hit" count and show "jūsu trīs biežākās".
- **20.2.c** Build the simulator: tier declaration, N items sampled without recent repeats, timer, per-tier scoring,
      55 % threshold, and a result screen that links every wrong answer to its explanation and seed.

### Subtask 20.3 — Escape hatches and print
- **20.3.a** Implement export (textarea + copy button), import (paste + validate + merge or replace choice), and
      reset (double confirmation). No file downloads required; a copyable string is enough and works offline.
- **20.3.b** Implement the flashcard print sheet: a print-only section with 43 prompts, 4 per page, answers on a
      following page in the same order, with cut guides drawn as 1 px rules (not dashes).
- **20.3.c** Audit JS-off: every feature absent, the static ch16 list unchanged, and a note in ch16 explaining
      that the review loop needs JS and what to do without it.

### Gate
```bash
node build/check_storage.js                 # migration, corrupt, quota, round trip
python3 build/check_quiz.py                 # no answer leaks into summaries/index
node workspace_skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html --out /tmp/chem1/inspect
grep -c 'fetch(' Master_temats_1_skidumi_un_kimiskas_reakcijas.html   # 0
```

### Guardrails
- Do not turn the master into a game: no streaks, no badges, no confetti, no sound. `AGENTS.md` §6.3 says
  `learn-then-test` is for a *separate* quiz page if it is used at all; this task must therefore add the loop
  **inside** the existing page without importing the skill's chrome.
- Do not store anything by default. Opt-in for reading progress, and a visible "notīrīt manus datus".
- Do not let the dashboard become the page's first screen. It belongs in ch16.

| Community answers / comments | No backend, no moderation, no provenance |

| Multi-language toggle | The course is Latvian; a translation would double the claim surface with no reviewer |

# 4. The SVG standard (normative)

This is the short form of `build/SVG_STANDARD.md` that T10 must produce. It is written here so the standard can be
reviewed before any figure is redrawn. Rules use **must / should / may** in the RFC sense.

## 4.1 Canvas and geometry

1. **Must** declare `viewBox="0 0 760 H"` for full-width figures; the prerequisite DAG is the only exception
   (`0 0 560 618`) and **must** carry a comment saying why.
2. **Must** keep a 40-unit margin on all four sides; no element, leader or label may enter the margin.
3. **Should** align to a 20-unit baseline grid. Coordinates in `figures.py` **should** be computed from named
   constants, not typed as literals, when the layout is regular (tables, axes, grids).
4. **Must** set `height` only through the viewBox aspect ratio; no fixed `height` attribute.
5. **Must** avoid scaling below the declared `MIN_PX` (T12). Below it the figure switches to a scroll plate or a
   compact variant.
6. **Must** keep stroke widths in the 1 / 2 / 2.5 hierarchy defined in CSS classes; no inline `stroke-width`.

## 4.2 Type inside a figure

1. **Must** use exactly three sizes: `--fig-1` (data labels, axis ticks), `--fig-2` (annotations), `--fig-3`
   (in-figure headline). Today all five classes resolve to one size; that is the bug T10 fixes.
2. **Must not** use `font-size` attributes; sizes come from classes.
3. **Must** keep every label ≥ 12 user units on a 760-unit canvas (which is ≥ 11 px effective at the declared
   `MIN_PX`, and ≥ 7.5 pt in print).
4. **Should** use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for any text containing digits so columns line up.
5. **Must** write chemical formulas with `<tspan class="sub">` / `<tspan class="sup">` (or `dy` + size), never with
   Unicode subscript characters mixed with markup, and never with `baseline-shift` alone.
6. **Must** use the decimal comma, a thin no-break space before units, and U+2212 for minus, exactly as in body text.
7. **Must not** letter-space, italicise for decoration, or use small caps. Italics are reserved for quantities
   (*n*, *m*, *c*, ρ, α, *K*).
8. **Should** keep a line of text to ≤ 42 characters so it fits one line at the declared size.

## 4.3 Labels, leaders and legends

1. **Must** place labels outside the drawing area, in reserved bands. No label may sit inside a lobe, a cell, a
   circle or an arrow.
2. **Must** connect a label to its target with a straight `<path class="leader">`; the leader **must** stop ≥ 6
   units short of the target shape and **must not** cross another leader or a text bounding box.
3. **Must** align multi-line labels on one side (left or right), never centre-ragged into a drawing.
4. **Should** use numeric callouts (①②③) only when more than six leaders would be needed; in that case the callout
   **must** be explained in the caption, and the callout glyph **must** come from the text font, not an emoji.
5. **Must** include a legend only when a mark's meaning is not self-evident in context; the legend **must** sit
   adjacent to the drawing (not at the page bottom) and **must** survive print.
6. **Must not** repeat information already in the caption inside the drawing. The caption says what to notice; the
   drawing says what is.

## 4.4 Colour

1. **Must** use CSS custom properties for every `fill` and `stroke`; zero literal hex values in `figures.py`.
2. **Must** derive figure colours from the three semantic roles plus neutral tones; **may** add at most two data
   series colours (`--fig-data-1/2`) that are distinguishable in greyscale (ΔL* ≥ 15) and in deuteranopia.
3. **Must** achieve ≥ 4.5:1 for text on any filled shape, ≥ 3:1 for a shape's edge against its neighbour.
4. **Must not** use `opacity` below 1 on text. De-emphasis is expressed by a dashed outline, a lighter *tone from
   the token set*, or a word — never by fading text.
5. **Must** pair every colour-coded distinction with a second channel (label, hatch, dash). The pH strip is the one
   place where colour is the data, and it **must** carry the numbers beneath.
6. **Must** define print values for every token; a figure printed in greyscale **must** still be readable.

## 4.5 Data and correctness

1. **Must** take every number from `figdata.py`; a figure may not contain a constant that exists only in its drawing
   code.
2. **Must** assert those constants in `check_numbers.py` with the source page in the assertion message.
3. **Must** mark any value that is illustrative (a schematic curve, an interpolated point) as schematic in the
   caption — `fig-solubility` already does this for the lines between measured points; keep that honesty.
4. **Must** show a unit on every axis and in every data label, or state the unit in the axis title.
5. **Must not** draw a scale that implies precision the source does not have (e.g. a smooth curve through two
   points without saying it is schematic).
6. **Should** prefer a real `<table>` when the content is a comparison of ≥ 4 attributes (the matrix skill's rule);
   SVG is for shapes, tables are for cells.

## 4.6 Accessibility and semantics

1. **Must** have `role="img"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at a unique `<title>` id, and an `aria-describedby`-
   equivalent `<desc>`.
2. **Must** write `<title>` as the figure's name and `<desc>` as *what to notice*, not what is drawn.
3. **Must** keep ids unique across the whole page (16 figures × 2 ids today; the build asserts it).
4. **Must** be usable with JS off and printable with all labels visible.
5. **Must** expose an interactive mode (if any) through a labelled control, keyboard-operable, with state announced
   once.
6. **Should** keep decorative vectors `aria-hidden` and out of the reading order.

## 4.7 Motion

1. **Must** limit motion to state transitions of a scrubber or a mask, ≤ 160 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`.
2. **Must** honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by switching to an instant state change.
3. **Must not** animate a data value (no tweening numbers, no growing bars on scroll).

## 4.8 Review checklist (per figure, before merge)

- [ ] Data: every number from `figdata.py`, asserted, unit present.
- [ ] Geometry: inside the viewBox, 40-unit margin, 20-unit grid where regular.
- [ ] Type: three sizes max, ≥ 12 units, tabular digits, real sub/sup.
- [ ] Labels: outside the drawing, leaders straight, no crossings, no text over a shape.
- [ ] Colour: tokens only, contrast measured, second channel present, print values defined.
- [ ] Semantics: title, desc ("what to notice"), unique ids, caption with source or *papildinājums*.
- [ ] Responsiveness: ≥ 11 px effective at 390 (or a declared compact variant), no page-level overflow.
- [ ] Print: §4.4.6 and §4.5; no split, no clip, ≥ 7.5 pt.
- [ ] Interaction (if any): keyboard, `aria-expanded`, static transcript for no-JS and print.
- [ ] One retrieval prompt next to it in the chapter.

# 6. Sequencing, dependencies and how to run this without breaking it

## 6.1 Waves

```
Wave 1 (fix the truth)        T01  T02  T03
Wave 2 (decide the look)      T04  T05  T06          depends on W1
Wave 3 (make it navigable)    T07  T08  T09          depends on W2 (T07 also on T04)
Wave 4 (fix the drawing system) T10 T11 T12          depends on W2
Wave 5 (draw the missing pictures) T13 T14 T15       depends on W4
Wave 6 (fix the explanation, then the edges) T16 T17 T18 T19   depends on W1, T03, T10–T15
Wave 7 (study loop)           T20                    depends on T07, T09, T16, T17
```

**Why this order.** Every later task edits Latvian text or figures; T01 fixes the terms, T03 makes the gate honest,
and T10 fixes the drawing system. Doing T13 before T10 means redrawing 6 figures twice. Doing T20 before T07 means
building a dashboard with nowhere to put it.

**Critical path:** T01 → T03 → T10 → T11 → T13/T14/T15 → T16 → T20.

## 6.2 File ownership (a hard rule while agents work in parallel)

| File(s) | Single owner during a wave |
| --- | --- |
| `build/terms.py`, `build/content/ch*.html` (text) | the T01 agent, then handed over |
| `build/check.sh`, `build/gate.py`, `build/exceptions.json`, `build/check-report.json` | the T03 agent **only**; everyone else asks it for a step |
| `build/assets/style.css`, `build/typography.py` | the T05/T06 agent (one agent, not two) |
| `build/figures.py`, `build/figdata.py`, `build/SVG_STANDARD.md` | the T10 agent, then the T13/T14/T15 agents in sequence |
| `build/build_master.py` | the T07 agent during W3, the T08 agent during W3 (coordinate: two changes, one file) |
| `build/quiz.py` | the T17 agent |
| `build/prereq.py`, `build/definitions.py` | untouched unless T16 changes a first use |

If two tasks must touch one file, they run in the same worktree, sequentially, by the same agent. Never "merge
later".

## 6.3 What every task must leave behind

1. A gate step that would fail if the defect returned (except T13–T15, which inherit T11).
2. A line in `build/README.md` (the file already documents each subsystem — keep that habit).
3. Evidence in `build/evidence/`: screenshots, measured tables, before/after numbers.
4. A changelog entry in ch17 (`#žurnāls`) with what changed and which ledger id motivated it.
5. No change to the built HTML by hand. The build is the only writer.

## 6.4 Parallel-agent protocol (if a workflow is used)

- **Do not** fan out over chapters for T16. Prose rewrites need one voice; splitting by chapter produces 17 voices.
- **Do** fan out over *measurement* (T11 audit, T19 a11y audit, T12 legibility table) — those are read-only and
  independent.
- **Do** fan out over *figure drawing* once the standard is frozen: one agent per figure, each with the checklist in
  §4.8, all in separate worktrees, integrated by the T10 owner.
- Any agent that writes must run its own gate before returning; a summary without a passing gate is not evidence.

## 7.2 The human checks (no script replaces these)

1. Open the file from disk with JS off; read one whole chapter; note every moment where you have to scroll back.
2. Print the whole document and read 10 pages — including one with a matrix, one with a figure, one with a
   correction pair.
3. Tab from the top to the contents; count the stops. If it is more than 5, T07 failed.
4. Search for "šķīdība" with and without the macron; both must find the chapter.
5. Ask a student (or simulate one) to answer B #13 using only the page; watch where they get stuck. That is the
   real score for T16/T17.

## 7.3 Definition of "done" for the whole programme

- `lint.mjs` 0 FAIL, `inspect.mjs` 0 FAIL **with an empty exception list except the declared, reasoned ones**.
- `gate.py` and `check.sh` agree, and both print the exception register.
- 0 HTML structural errors, 0 duplicate ids, 0 leftover placeholders.
- 33 figures (16 today + 17 new from T13–T15), all passing the audit; 25 is the floor if the new-figure tasks are
  partially cut, in which case the cut figures are named in the final report rather than silently dropped.
- All 61 E ids shown; all 32 mistake seeds placed; the count of `[jāpārbauda]` reported one per line.
- Search finds any glossary term in ≤ 2 keystrokes after the first character.
- The print PDF opens with every answer visible and correct page numbers.
- The final report (`MASTER_PROMPT.md` §10) is regenerated from `check-report.json`, not typed by hand.

# 9. Do-not-do list (guards against the obvious wrong fixes)

1. **Do not** add raster photography to satisfy `few-pictures`. The subject is notation; the honest answer is a
   reasoned exception plus better diagrams.
2. **Do not** introduce a gradient, a shadow, a grain overlay, a glass panel or a rounded-card system. All are in
   the earlier master's 31 FAILs.
3. **Do not** number sections with medallions or coordinate labels; the numbering lives in the contents and the
   cross-references.
4. **Do not** replace body prose with accordions. Depth is optional; the exam core is never hidden.
5. **Do not** make the page shorter by deleting sourcing, corrections or the id tags. Those are the product.
6. **Do not** "fix" a source error without showing it (no silent corrections, ever).
7. **Do not** invent a clinical range, an exam question "from the course", a lecturer quote, or a citation.
8. **Do not** tune a threshold (overlap %, WARN baseline, font floor) until the build goes green.
9. **Do not** run two agents on one file in one worktree.
10. **Do not** declare a task complete on a summary. The gate output is the completion criterion.
